LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Denver Broncos play host to the Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos are coming off their third win in the last four games, though it required a late, game-winning drive against the decrepit division rival Los Angeles Chargers . The return of Sean Payton as play-caller didn't exactly result in an explosive or efficient offense, but the Broncos did just enough to hold off L.A. and climb back over .500. The Seahawks, meanwhile, dropped to 3-2 after falling to their own division rivals in the San Francisco 49ers . The Niners moved the ball quite well against the vaunted Seattle defense, and turnovers in their own territory haunted the Seahawks and ultimately cost them the game. Will the Seahawks bounce back, or will the Broncos capture their second consecutive victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Broncos vs. Seahawks live Date: Thursday, Oct. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Empower Field at Mile High (Denver) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Seahawks have the ball Let's start here: the Seahawks cannot run the ball at all. They couldn't run the ball when rookie running back Jadarian Price was healthy earlier in the season, and they haven't been able to run the ball since he's been out. The trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has combined for just 447 yards on 127 carries -- an average of just 3.5 per tote. The Seahawks do not get much push up front, as their backs average a mere 0.69 yards before contact per carry, a figure that ranks fourth-worst in the NFL , according to Tru Media. Their 2.83 yards after contact per carry is more respectable, ranking 14th league-wide. The Broncos will have to be careful there. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league so far (0.59), but the most rushing yards after contact (3.92), thanks to a sky-high avoided tackle rate by enemy backs (30.1%). Much of that production came from Kenneth Walker III in the season opener, but even in Weeks 2 through 5, the Broncos rank in the bottom third of the league in both yards after contact per attempt and broken tackle rate. Wilson is likely to be the primary runner once again while Price and Zach Charbonnet remain sidelined. The Broncos will have to get him on the ground on the first try, limiting the yards he can gain after contact, because the Seahawks just don't create much for him in the first place. He scarcely gets more than is blocked without breaking through tackles. In the passing game, Sam Darnold has struggled to replicate last year's results -- especially over the last two weeks. In games against the Chargers and 49ers, Darnold went just 31-of-51 for 363 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. After leading the league in turnovers last season, Darnold has already been picked off five times in his three full appearances this season, while his yards per attempt average is down from 8.5 to just 7.7. His completion rate is down over 3 percentage points as well. Denver's pass defense has been largely good so far this year, with the Broncos ranking fifth in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media. The Broncos just held the Chargers to 82 net passing yards last week, which plays a huge role in that figure, but they've also allowed only one team ( Rams ) to top 218 net passing yards in any game so far. (The Chiefs didn't have to throw the ball very much in Week 1, though, because they did whatever they wanted on the ground.) The Broncos won't have Patrick Surtain II or Talanoa Hufanga here, and Riley Moss is listed as questionable -- all of which is a significant issue when you're going up against Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL in both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine figure to see increased roles due to the cornerback injuries, while Devon Key will play more in the wake of Hufanga's absence. They'll all have their work cut out for them against JSN. The Seahawks really don't throw the ball to anyone else all that often. When the Broncos have the ball Denver might have gotten a win last week, but Sean Payton's return as play-caller didn't have much to do with it. The Broncos entered the game against the Chargers averaging a miserable 4.9 yards per play, then averaged a mere 3.9 per play in the win over Los Angeles. Bo Nix totaled just 123 yards on his 27 pass attempts, J.K. Dobbins ran for only 68 yards on his 18 carries, Jaylen Waddle caught just two of five balls thrown his way for just 19 yards ... nothing went well offensively. And nothing has gone right pretty much all year, with the exception of the second halves of the Broncos' wins over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3. Two good halves in five weeks isn't much to write home about, even if those halves helped the Broncos steal a pair of wins and arrive at 3-2. Nix is essentially refusing to push the ball down the field so far this season. His average air yards per attempt in each of his first two years of his career was 7.3, according to Tru Media, but that figure has dropped all the way to 5.2 this year. He threw deep on 13.1% of his passes as a rookie and 11.8% of them last year, but he's done so on only 7.4% of his attempts this season. Nix also isn't running anymore. He scrambled 27.3% of the time when pressured during his rookie season and 16.1% of the time last season. That number is all the way down to 5.6% so far this year, meaning he's scrambled only four times in five games. All of this, combined with his insistence on checking down repeatedly, has made the pass offense feel neutered to date. Meanwhile, the Broncos also can't run the ball. Dobbins looks like he's running with a piano on his back, slogging his way to 3.6 yards per carry. RJ Harvey barely gets opportunities, but he hasn't done any better at only 3.7 yards per carry. Harvey is at least productive in the short passing game, but the Broncos de-emphasized that last week under Payton in favor of more Dobbins runs that went nowhere. The Seahawks have largely been their usual selves defensively through the first five weeks of the season. They've arrived at their two losses largely by virtue of their offense repeatedly turning the ball over against the Commanders (three times) and 49ers (four, including a fumble that resulted in a touchdown). Seattle has held opponents to the fewest passing yards in the league and the fewest net yards per attempt, and it has limited running games to the eighth-fewest yards per attempt as well. It's hard to see the Broncos snapping out of their funk against this unit. Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have let the Broncos come away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Surtain here, which is obviously a problem against JSN. Denver and Seattle both have playoff expectations – and Super Bowl hopes – in the 2026 season, but their offenses have to improve to make those dreams a reality. With Denver banged up a bit in the secondary on Thursday, Seattle has a shot to get back on track. It won’t be easy, though, as the Broncos are 2-0 at home with impressive victories against Jacksonville and the Los Angeles Rams. The Seahawks rank second in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate, while the Broncos rank 10th and sixth in those two metrics. Denver's defensive numbers are that good while having played some of the best offenses in the league to begin the season, including the Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, and 49ers, so expect them to improve their standing in their defensive analytics soon. Meanwhile, I have some question marks about both offenses. They rank 24th and 26th in EPA per play, and Seattle's offense is in a tough spot, having to play at altitude in Denver on a short week. The Broncos are fifth in the NFL in EPA/Pass, but Sam Darnold has locked in on JSN all season long, so I don’t expect his target share to waver. The defending World Champion Seattle Seahawks are coming to Mile High for a Thursday Night Football throwdown. It's a short-week turnaround for both teams, with the Broncos coming off a win and the Seahawks off a loss. Broncos-Seahawks was the Super Bowl many people expected last season before Bo Nix's shocking ankle injury. When the 2026 schedule dropped earlier this year, this game was circled as a potential Super Bowl preview. Despite both teams sitting at 3-2, few people currently view the Broncos as a true Super Bowl contender, but that's no different than the general consensus at this time last year. The narrative around the Seahawks, though, is strikingly different. What's the disconnect? Offense. The Broncos' offense and the quality of quarterback play haven't been at a Super Bowl level — but the season is still young. How will Broncos-Seahawks shake out on Thursday night? We're going around the table to see how the Denver Broncos On SI / Mile High Huddle staff foresee this one playing out at Mile High. You can connect with each staff on X (their handles are linked next to their names). Also without a status, despite being listed as limited all week with an ankle injury, is defensive lineman Leonard Williams, who played last week through the injury he suffered in a Week 4 win over the Chargers. Also ruled out are linebacker Chazz Surratt, who will miss a third straight game with a calf injury, and running back Zach Charbonnet, who remains on the physically unable to perform list as he works his way back from the torn ACL he suffered in last season's Divisional Round win over the 49ers. For the Broncos, All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II has been ruled out with an ankle injury, as has starting safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle). The Denver Broncos' defense has remained dominant this season, buoying a head-scratching offense through a month-plus of competition. Coordinated by Vance Joseph, the unit has picked up right where it left off a season ago. It's receiving a midseason reinforcement, too. The NFL announced Friday that it's removing outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper from the commissioner exempt list. Cooper, who missed the first six games of the 2026 campaign following a pair of domestic incidents, will be eligible to play for the 4-2 Broncos in their Week 7 road game against the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 25. "The NFL initiated an investigation under the personal conduct policy following Cooper's arrests in June," a league statement reads, via NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . "The league's review remains ongoing and is not affected by this change to Cooper's roster status." Cooper, 28, was initially arrested on June 4 . That's when police were called to his apartment in the wake of an altercation with his then-girlfriend. As previously reported by The Athletic, further examination of the incident, including consideration of a report from a nurse who evaluated the woman the night of the alleged domestic violence, resulted in Cooper facing a felony charge of second-degree assault by strangulation. Back then, the nurse wrote in her report that the woman sustained "serious bodily injury" consistent with "strangulation with hypoxia" and "traumatic brain injury," per The Athletic, which cited an arrest affidavit in its reporting. Cooper's second arrest in a seven-day span took place on June 11. That time, he was booked on a charge of violating a protection order put in place after the aforementioned incident. On Aug. 31, the 2021 seventh-round pick from Ohio State pleaded not guilty to all five charges against him . The day prior, he landed on the commissioner exempt list. Notably, Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was also removed from that list on Friday . On Sept. 10, less than four months after a domestic abuse arrest , Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property . He was reportedly convicted of battery and fined $1,000. Additionally, per ESPN , the 28-year-old Jacobs accepted a deferred judgment agreement on the criminal damage to property charge. home.blurb: One of the first injuries was suffered by running back Tyler Badie, who injured his thumb in the second quarter and was ruled out just before halftime. The severity of Badie's injury is not yet known, but rookie running back Jonah Coleman ( ankle ) is eligible to return from injured reserve next week. On offense, wide receiver Jaylen Waddle ( shoulder ) left the sideline early to go into the locker room just before halftime. Waddle, who was announced as questionable, returned in the third quarter and finished the game. Fellow receiver Courtland Sutton appeared to have a slight limp after he took a huge hit, but he also finished the game. After playing on TNF this week, the Broncos have 10 days before their next game against the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 25. That extra time could prove to be helpful for the club's injured players. After a long weekend, Denver will return to practice and begin releasing injury reports next Wednesday. Broncos defensive lineman Malcolm Roach was evaluated in the team's blue medical tent late in the second quarter, but he returned to the game in the second half and ended the night with a team-high four quarterback hits. Elsewhere on the defensive line, D.J. Jones was spotted holding his left hand in pain, but he also finished the game. What appeared to be the most concerning injury of the night was suffered by outside linebacker Jonah Elliss late in the fourth quarter. After the play, Elliss limped off the field, favoring his right leg to avoid forcing the Broncos to call a timeout and stop the clock while the Seahawks were attempting to get within field goal range. Elliss was then carted off the sideline. Note that the replay of his injury is gruesome: We're still awaiting news on the severity of Elliss' injury. Houston finally broke through by beating Tennessee 26-3, then acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. These predictions deliberately push beyond a narrow upset or another respectable quarterback performance. The forecast: Houston produces its most complete game of the season. Conversely, they allow an NFL-best 63.8 rushing yards per game and just 2.9 yards per carry. Houston therefore has good reason to attack through Stroud rather than repeatedly challenge Jacksonville's strongest area. Stroud has already thrown for 1,402 yards with six touchdowns and no interceptions through five games. Against Tennessee, he completed 26 of 34 attempts for 261 yards, including an impressive eight completions on 11 pressured throws for 115 yards. The prediction requires Houston to convert passing volume into touchdowns, something it has not consistently accomplished. Harrison's arrival creates another possible weapon, although his debut and workload remain uncertain. This call rests primarily on Stroud's existing production and Jacksonville's passing-yardage vulnerability, not an assumption that the newcomer immediately dominates. Will Anderson Jr. records four sacks as Houston forces three turnovers Anderson delivered three of Houston's four sacks against Tennessee, providing the foundation for an even bigger prediction against Jacksonville. Four sacks by one player would be a spectacular follow-up, not merely continued improvement. The Texans limited the Titans to 187 total yards and three points after DeMeco Ryans reclaimed defensive play-calling duties. Tennessee's struggling offense makes that result an imperfect measuring stick, but Houston still ranks ninth in yards allowed per play. Jacksonville presents a tougher opponent, yet Sunday exposed pressure points. Trevor Lawrence threw an interception and lost a fumble against Philadelphia despite producing 331 passing yards and two touchdowns. Houston must turn disruptive plays into possession changes, rather than simply allowing Jacksonville to reset after sacks. The Jaguars' penalty problems could help create those opportunities. They have committed at least 13 penalties and accumulated more than 100 penalty yards in consecutive games. Backward movement makes passing situations more predictable, giving Anderson additional chances to attack. The bold call is four Anderson sacks and three Houston takeaways: pressure converts Jacksonville's mistakes into decisive field-position advantages. The Texans win by at least 17 points Jacksonville's winning record and scoring defense make a comfortable Houston victory the biggest leap here. The Jaguars have allowed only 70 points across five games, while the Texans entered last Sunday without a win. Nevertheless, a blowout becomes plausible if the first two predictions connect. Houston's passing offense attacks Jacksonville's statistical weakness, while turnovers supply short fields and prevent Lawrence from answering every score. Jacksonville also needed a 53-yard kickoff return and Cam Little's 57-yard field goal to escape Philadelphia. That extraordinary finish demonstrated resilience, but it should not conceal how close the Jaguars came to losing. Stroud's four touchdown passes power the offense, and defensive disruption keeps the Jaguars from turning their rushing balance into sustained control. London delivers a division-changing upset, not another last-second escape. away.headline: The Texans Injury Situation Ahead of Sunday's Titans Game
away.blurb: For the Titans, Carnell Tate (back), Joshua Williams (pec) and David Martin-Robinson (hamstring) were all questionable. Tate and Williams have been cleared by Robert Saleh, while Martin-Robinson is still a game-time decision. Williams still has to be added to the active roster. Amani Hooker is out with a concussion. The Titans were otherwise free of any other injuries. The Texans have more than one game-time decision. Receiver Tank Dell is obviously still out with his knee injury. He was limited for two days of practice and didn't practice on Friday. M.J. Stewart (Knee), Blake Fisher (illness), Braden Smith (foot), Ed Ingram (illness), Aireontae Ersery (illness) and Kayden McDonald (ankle) were all questionable on the Texans' final injury report. Out of those players above, Ersery and Ingram are starters on the offensive line. Smith, McDonald, and Stewart would need to be activated from injured reserve. Fisher isn't a starter but could be one of the next men up if Ersery can't play. The Titans are definitely in better shape than the Texans with their injuries. The Texans have 13 players on the IR right now. Stewart, McDonald, Dell and Smith have all been designated for return but must be activated first. The Texans Injury Situation Ahead of Sunday's Titans Game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL The Texans Injury Situation Ahead of Sunday's Titans Game (Andrew Nelles / The Tennessean) Grant Bricker Sat, October 10, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Tennessee Titans and Houston Texans are meeting for the 49th time in series history on Sunday. The series is tied at 24, and something's got to give. Both teams are 0-4 and searching for that elusive first win of the season. The Titans and Texans have had many close games this year. Outside of the 23-10 loss to the New York Jets in the season opener, the Titans have lost the last three games by six points or fewer. The Texans are in the same boat. They lost a 36-31 shootout with the Buffalo Bills in their season opener. Then, they lost to Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals 20-6. The Indianapolis Colts beat the Texans 19-17 on a go-ahead field goal with 16 seconds left. Last week, the Texans lost a heartbreaker to the Dallas Cowboys 34-30. Now, either the Titans or the Texans will get their first win on Sunday. Ahead of the game, both teams released their final injury reports . Tennessee has eight players on its IR. Fernando Carmona and Jackson Slater are the most recent additions. They joined Jaylen Harrell, Jaren Kanak, Dorian Mausi, Tanoh Kpassagnon, Milo Eifler, and Kendell Brooks. Injuries are going to happen in football. It's unfortunately a reality of playing at this level. The Texans are dealing with more than the Titans are heading into Sunday. That won't guarantee a win, but it's one advantage the Titans have. Kickoff is set for noon CT on CBS.

home.headline: Jaguars turn to Jacob Bobenmoyer after Ross Matiscik injury: Report
home.blurb: NFL MLB NBA NHL NCAA Football NCAA Basketball UFC/MMA PGA Tour Games JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS Jaguars sign Jacob Bobenmoyer to practice squad after Matiscik injury Jacob Bobenmoyer will take over snapping duties after DaVon Hamilton's emergency stint, per report. This story was updated to add new information. The Jacksonville Jaguars have found a replacement for defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton , who served as the team's long snapper for most of Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles in London. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Monday that the long snapper was arriving shortly, and he's now at The Grove with the rest of the team. According to NFL Media's Ian Rapoport, the Jaguars will sign veteran long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer , while typical starting long snapper Ross Matiscik recovers from a shoulder injury sustained in the first quarter against Philly. Who is long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer, Ross Matiscik's replacement? Bobenmoyer, 29, has spent seven years in the NFL with two teams: the Denver Broncos (2019-2022) and the Las Vegas Raiders (2023-2025). Bobenmoyer has played 97 games, recording 22 tackles and 1 fumble recovery. Jacksonville is currently overseas in London as it prepares to play its second of two matchups across the pond. The Jaguars will take on the Houston Texans in Week 6. According to Rapoport, Bobenmoyer has already flown to London. Hamilton stepped in for Jacksonville after Matiscik was injured. Teams typically carry only one long snapper on their 53-man roster or practice squad. Sunday's win marked the second time Hamilton served as the team's long snapper after Matiscik's injury. Hamilton helped set up Cam Little 's game-winning 57-yard field goal . Although Hamilton's snap was high, punter Logan Cooke got the ball down quickly, giving Little time to boot it through the uprights. The Jaguars won in the final seconds against the Eagles, 19-17. The Jaguars (4-1) will face off against the Texans in Week 6 at Wembley Stadium as they look to bury their division rival. The Texans are currently 1-4 after netting their first win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 5. Demetrius Harvey is the Jacksonville Jaguars reporter for the Florida Times-Union. You can follow him on X (formerly Twitter) at @Demetrius82 or on Bluesky at Demetrius .

Yes. Yes. Let me say it again: Yes. After a horror show in Week 4 with my NFL picks , I got back on track in a big way this past week. I was 10-4-1 straight up and 9-6-1 against the spread. That brings my season record straight up to 48-30-1 and the ATS record to 34-43-2. The ATS mark will be a slow climb to get back above .500 after that really bad Week 3. But I felt good about the picks this week. Time to build some momentum. Two good weeks in a row? All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Houston Texans at Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) London on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Jaguars will have been in London for two weeks, which makes this a challenge for the Texans , who went this week. Houston won for the first time on the road last week and now their division chances probably rest on this game. The Jaguars were sloppy last week, which will get them back focused. Jaguars will win a tight one. Pick: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears at Atlanta Falcons (+3) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a horrible showing in Green Bay, in which the defense was shredded. But the Falcons lost in overtime to the Ravens and quarterback Michael Penix was hurt. He will likely play here, and that's a good thing since he can light up the Chicago defense. Falcons win it. Pick: Falcons 27, Bears 21 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns There is a chance that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will be back for this game after missing last week with an ankle injury. Even if he isn't, I think the Ravens defense will be up to the task of slowing down the Browns offense. If Jackson is back, the Ravens offense will move the ball. Pick: Ravens 24, Browns 13 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts (-7) The winless Titans head out on the road to play a Colts team that has been inconsistent. The Colts' defense has improved in recent weeks, which will challenge Cam Ward and the Titans' limited offense. Look for the Colts to get a division victory as Jonathan Taylor has a big game. Pick: Colts 28, Titans 17 New York Jets at New England Patriots (-7.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Patriots have turned their season around with consecutive victories as Drake Maye has come alive. The Jets played better on defense against Cleveland last week with eight sacks, but this is a bigger challenge. Look for Maye to keep it going as the Pats win a third straight. Pick: Patriots 28, Jets 13 New Orleans Saints at New York Giants (+1.5) The Saints have lost three straight and have fallen to 1-4. They didn't play well against the Vikings last week, but this is a chance to get right. The Giants tied last week, but Jameis Winston played well. I think this will be about defenses. Giants in a close one. Pick: Giants 19, Saints 16 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense. Pick: Eagles 23, Panthers 20 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+3) Both of these teams righted the ship a bit with victories last week. The Bucs badly needed it after losing their first four. Tampa Bay ran it with Bucky Irving to beat the Cowboys and I think they can do that here as well. The defense played better in that game and will limit Aaron Rodgers somewhat. Bucs win it. Pick: Bucs 26, Steelers 21 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams (-13.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The "Dream Team" Rams are 2-3 and haven't looked the part of a Super Bowl champ. The offense got it going against the Bills , but the defense was a non-factor in the fourth quarter and overtime. They will play better here against the Cardinals . Meanwhile, Matt Stafford will have a big day. Pick: Rams 35, Cardinals 20 Los Angeles Chargers (+8.5) at Kansas City Chiefs Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chargers limp into this one at 0-5, while the Chiefs are undefeated off a bye. The Chargers are desperate and need a win or their season will be over. This is not a good place to try to get that first victory. Look for Patrick Mahomes to play well. Chiefs coach Andy Reid is outstanding in his career off a bye. Pick: Chiefs 28, Chargers 21 Buffalo Bills (-6) at Las Vegas Raiders The Bills are playing consecutive road games, but they stayed on the West Coast after beating the Rams in overtime Monday night. That was a tough, physical game, which will make it a challenge on a short week. The Raiders were awful against the Pats, but they will play better on offense here. They just won't stop the Bills. Pick: Bills 35, Raiders 21 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Packers blew out the Bears Sunday as Jordan Love lit up the skies. Look for more of that in this one against a bad Dallas secondary. The Cowboys struggled on defense against the Bucs, and that will continue in this one. Love continues to play well. Packers win a shootout. Pick: Packers 31, Cowboys 27 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a long road trip for the Commanders off a brutal tie last week to face the league's best team right now. That's a tough combination. They can only hope for a letdown by the 49ers after they beat Seattle last week. It won't happen. The 49ers continue to roll as Brock Purdy continues to make a claim as a legitimate MVP candidate. Pick: 49ers 30, Commanders 21 Seattle Seahawks (-3) at Denver Broncos Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Seahawks lost a tough one to the 49ers last week and now face a short week on the road against Denver. The Broncos ' offense has struggled, even with Sean Payton taking over as the play-caller. Bo Nix has to pick it up, but this is a tough defense to try and fix things. Seattle takes a tough road game. Chicago is now 3-2 this season, and it appears Williams is nearing a return from the hamstring strain (Grade 2) that he suffered in Week 2 against the Minnesota Vikings. According to Bears head coach Ben Johnson, Williams is "on track" and he believes it'll be "close" if he's able to play in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. That's something that seems hard to bounce back from, because everyone looks dumb. Minter said that Lamar Jackson remains “day to day” and when he’s ready, he’ll be out at practice. While BetMGM has priced Sunday’s game with the expectation that Jackson will be in the lineup, not every book has done so. away.headline: Browns get much-needed injury boost ahead of Ravens showdown
away.blurb: All four players returned to practice Friday, according to ESPN’s Daniel Oyefusi. Their return raises the possibility that all four could play in the pivotal division matchup vs. the Baltimore Ravens. Without Judkins, Cleveland would likely lean on Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime, who joined the team from Minnesota’s practice squad this week. Dylan Sampson’s potential return could also affect the backfield. Judkins’ return to practice offers encouragement for a Browns rushing attack still searching for consistency. Arguably, the three most important players to return to practice are Mason Graham, Carson Schwesinger, and Derek Barnett. Graham got hurt during the Browns' Thursday Night Football game vs. the Pittsburgh Steelers in a scary injury many thought would take him out for multiple weeks. Now, just two weeks later, the star defensive tackle has returned to practice. Having Graham, Schwesinger, and Barnett available matters because the Browns need to stop the run against one of the league's best backs, Derrick Henry . The Ravens' starting quarterback, Lamar Jackson, hasn't practiced all week leading up to the Browns matchup. Considering the Browns allowed 134 rushing yards just a week ago to a less talented Jets team, Henry will get his fair share of carries. Graham missed that matchup, and having him available alongside Schwesinger and Barnett would give Cleveland a better chance to contain Baltimore’s ground game. The Browns now have several key players back at practice ahead of Sunday’s matchup with the Ravens. With Lamar Jackson, the Ravens' MVP quarterback, potentially unavailable Sunday, the Browns have a real chance to reclaim the AFC North. The Cleveland Browns have a chance to top the AFC North again. Luckily for them, they just received big injury news. The Browns lost to the New York Jets in Week 5 of the NFL season in a sloppy, rainy game. Cleveland emerged from the loss with additional injury concerns and opened Week 6 with 17 players on its injury report. Important players on that list included Carson Schewsinger, Mason Graham, Quinshon Judkins, and Derek Barnett. The Browns' run game has been less than desirable early in the NFL season. However, those struggles could worsen Sunday if the Browns are without their lead back, Quinshon Judkins. The question now is whether the team will rise to the occasion as it did in Weeks 2 through 4 or fumble an opportunity as it did in Weeks 1 and 5. away.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
away.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. away.headline: Lamar Jackson injury update, latest rumors on Ravens QB's status for NFL Week 6 vs. Browns
away.blurb: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Jackson's status Friday, ruling him out for the matchup. Adam Schefter of ESPN has previously reported that Jackson had a "realistic chance to return for Sunday's game, with Minter telling reporters that Jackson was considered day-to-day. Minter added that Jackson is "working his butt off" and "doing everything he can" to return to the field. Jackson was out for Week 5 as Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns as he continues to recover from an ankle injury. He initially left Week 4's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury and didn't play in the second half, a concerning development for a Ravens' offense very much reliant on the dynamic quarterback's unique skill set. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported the Ravens are "hopeful" Trey Hendrickson—who has missed two games with a thumb injury—returns this week. While the Ravens didn't believe at the time that Jackson's injury was going to be a long-term issue, there was uncertainty over his short-term availability. "I really don't think it's going to be crazy long term, but we'll see what happens," head coach Jesse Minter told reporters at the time. There's no replacing a two-time MVP and three-time first-team All-Pro like Jackson, though the Ravens do have an experienced backup in Huntley. "There's one Lamar Jackson, the guy's a two-time MVP," Minter said after Week 4. "And so I think for anybody to have to say we're being compared to Lamar is unfair and not realistic. I think [Huntley] as a backup quarterback in this league and even as a starter at times has shown the ability to come in and really kind of run the offense, make plays with his legs, be able to make plays on third down." Injuries were also a concern for Jackson last season, as he missed four games due to a hamstring injury and a back contusion. Huntley started two of those games, leading the team to a 2-0 record. But the Ravens are obviously a much more dangerous team with a healthy Jackson.

They are all listed as questionable for Sunday. Rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion also cleared concussion protocol and is expected to play. Defensive tackles Mike Hall (ankle), Kalia Davis (quad) and guard Teven Jenkins (back) were all ruled out after not practicing Friday. Running back Dylan Sampson (knee), who was designated to return from injured reserve this week, was also ruled out, as was quarterback Dillon Gabriel, who continues to recover from a back injury. It will mark the second straight game he has missed. The two-time NFL Most Valuable Player has not practiced since suffering an ankle injury late in the second quarter on Oct. 4 in a win over the Tennessee Titans. “It’s day by day,” Minter said when asked whether Jackson was close to playing this week. “I think it’s just a decision for his best interest.” Tyler “Snoop” Huntley, who led Baltimore (4-1) to a 30-23 overtime win over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, will get the start. Huntley is 3-0 as the starter over the past two seasons and 8-9 in his career. The Ravens are 7-11 in games Jackson has missed since he became the starter in 2019. Huntley is also coming off one of his best career games. Against the Falcons, he completed 24 of 32 passes for 201 yards and two touchdowns. He also rushed for another score. Huntley completed his final 11 passes on back-to-back scoring drives at the end of regulation and in overtime. Now, he has two full weeks of practice under his belt. It has also helped that Jackson has been a willing communicator during games, giving Huntley insight into what he has seen on certain plays. home.headline: Browns get much-needed injury boost ahead of Ravens showdown
home.blurb: All four players returned to practice Friday, according to ESPN’s Daniel Oyefusi. Their return raises the possibility that all four could play in the pivotal division matchup vs. the Baltimore Ravens. Without Judkins, Cleveland would likely lean on Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime, who joined the team from Minnesota’s practice squad this week. Dylan Sampson’s potential return could also affect the backfield. Judkins’ return to practice offers encouragement for a Browns rushing attack still searching for consistency. Arguably, the three most important players to return to practice are Mason Graham, Carson Schwesinger, and Derek Barnett. Graham got hurt during the Browns' Thursday Night Football game vs. the Pittsburgh Steelers in a scary injury many thought would take him out for multiple weeks. Now, just two weeks later, the star defensive tackle has returned to practice. Having Graham, Schwesinger, and Barnett available matters because the Browns need to stop the run against one of the league's best backs, Derrick Henry . The Ravens' starting quarterback, Lamar Jackson, hasn't practiced all week leading up to the Browns matchup. Considering the Browns allowed 134 rushing yards just a week ago to a less talented Jets team, Henry will get his fair share of carries. Graham missed that matchup, and having him available alongside Schwesinger and Barnett would give Cleveland a better chance to contain Baltimore’s ground game. The Browns now have several key players back at practice ahead of Sunday’s matchup with the Ravens. With Lamar Jackson, the Ravens' MVP quarterback, potentially unavailable Sunday, the Browns have a real chance to reclaim the AFC North. The Cleveland Browns have a chance to top the AFC North again. Luckily for them, they just received big injury news. The Browns lost to the New York Jets in Week 5 of the NFL season in a sloppy, rainy game. Cleveland emerged from the loss with additional injury concerns and opened Week 6 with 17 players on its injury report. Important players on that list included Carson Schewsinger, Mason Graham, Quinshon Judkins, and Derek Barnett. The Browns' run game has been less than desirable early in the NFL season. However, those struggles could worsen Sunday if the Browns are without their lead back, Quinshon Judkins. The question now is whether the team will rise to the occasion as it did in Weeks 2 through 4 or fumble an opportunity as it did in Weeks 1 and 5. home.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
home.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. home.headline: Lamar Jackson injury update, latest rumors on Ravens QB's status for NFL Week 6 vs. Browns
home.blurb: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Jackson's status Friday, ruling him out for the matchup. Adam Schefter of ESPN has previously reported that Jackson had a "realistic chance to return for Sunday's game, with Minter telling reporters that Jackson was considered day-to-day. Minter added that Jackson is "working his butt off" and "doing everything he can" to return to the field. Jackson was out for Week 5 as Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns as he continues to recover from an ankle injury. He initially left Week 4's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury and didn't play in the second half, a concerning development for a Ravens' offense very much reliant on the dynamic quarterback's unique skill set. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported the Ravens are "hopeful" Trey Hendrickson—who has missed two games with a thumb injury—returns this week. While the Ravens didn't believe at the time that Jackson's injury was going to be a long-term issue, there was uncertainty over his short-term availability. "I really don't think it's going to be crazy long term, but we'll see what happens," head coach Jesse Minter told reporters at the time. There's no replacing a two-time MVP and three-time first-team All-Pro like Jackson, though the Ravens do have an experienced backup in Huntley. "There's one Lamar Jackson, the guy's a two-time MVP," Minter said after Week 4. "And so I think for anybody to have to say we're being compared to Lamar is unfair and not realistic. I think [Huntley] as a backup quarterback in this league and even as a starter at times has shown the ability to come in and really kind of run the offense, make plays with his legs, be able to make plays on third down." Injuries were also a concern for Jackson last season, as he missed four games due to a hamstring injury and a back contusion. Huntley started two of those games, leading the team to a 2-0 record. But the Ravens are obviously a much more dangerous team with a healthy Jackson.

FanDuel Sportsbook is giving the Colts the edge against the winless Titans with a 6.5-point spread advantage. The money line is at -330 with the over/under starting at 43.5. picks.headline: Titans vs. Colts Preview: Indianapolis Looks to Bounce Back Against Winless Tennessee
picks.blurb: Titans vs. Colts Preview: Indianapolis Looks to Bounce Back Against Winless Tennessee - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Photo by: Charles LeClaire Stephan Stroud Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:13 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tennessee Titans travel to Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday to face the Indianapolis Colts in an AFC South matchup featuring two teams with very different starts to the 2026 NFL season. Tennessee enters Week 6 at 0-5 after suffering a disappointing 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans. Indianapolis is 2-3 following a 34-22 defeat against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Both teams are looking to respond, but the Titans desperately need their first victory of the season. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Cam Ward Looks to Spark Tennessee's Offense Titans quarterback Cam Ward remains the centerpiece of Tennessee's rebuilding effort. Despite the team's winless start, head coach Robert Saleh has continued to express confidence in the young quarterback and his ability to develop. Ward has completed 63.2% of his passes for 896 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions through five games. However, the Titans have struggled to generate consistent offense, scoring just three points against Houston last week. Tennessee needs Ward to make quicker decisions, protect the football and find ways to connect with his receivers downfield. Running back Tony Pollard will also be important. Establishing a productive ground game could take pressure off Ward and help Tennessee control possession against Indianapolis. Daniel Jones and Jonathan Taylor Lead Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones will look to guide Indianapolis back into the win column after the loss to Pittsburgh. Jones has thrown for 1,021 yards and three touchdowns this season, although four interceptions have contributed to some of the team's offensive inconsistency. Against Tennessee, protecting the football and taking advantage of scoring opportunities will be essential. The Colts also have one of the league's most dangerous running backs in Jonathan Taylor . Taylor has recorded 398 rushing yards and six touchdowns through five games, giving Indianapolis a reliable option to control the tempo. Wide receiver Josh Downs and tight end Tyler Warren provide Jones with additional receiving threats. Head coach Shane Steichen will look to create a balanced offensive attack that allows Taylor to establish the run while opening opportunities for Jones through the air. Can Tennessee Slow Down the Colts? The Titans' defense must find a way to contain Taylor and prevent Indianapolis from controlling the line of scrimmage. If Tennessee allows the Colts to establish their rushing attack early, Ward could face additional pressure to produce points quickly. Indianapolis, meanwhile, will try to pressure Ward into difficult decisions and capitalize on turnovers. A Crucial AFC South Battle Sunday presents an important opportunity for both teams. Tennessee is searching for its first win, while Indianapolis needs a response after consecutive losses. The Titans will need a more productive offensive performance from Ward, while the Colts will look to Taylor and Jones to lead the way. With both teams eager to get back on track, execution and ball security could determine the outcome of this divisional matchup.

away.headline: Colts' Week 6 injury report gives fans every reason to expect a Titans win
away.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts must feel pretty good about their health because they released Darius Slayton even though the team has struggled with wide receiver injuries this season. Not so much in Week 6, even though Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is going to be out and Alec Pierce still is . The positive is that Indy has a bye week, also known as having a matchup against the Tennessee Titans. As for Alec Pierce, no timeline exists for when he might return after reinjuring his heel. That might not happen until midseason, and the Colts will probably have far tougher games than the Titans before Pierce comes back. Besides Dulin, the only Indy player who will miss the game, according to head coach Shane Steichen , is linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs), but both Carlies and Dulin missed Week 5, and the reason the team lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers had nothing to do with the absences of Dulin and Carlies. The reason was that the defense was terrible again. Therein lies the difference between the Steelers and the Titans, as no matter how bad Indy's defense can be at times, Tennessee doesn't have the offensive talent that Pittsburgh has. Indianapolis Colts should be healthy enough to easily defeat the Tennessee Titans in Week 6 The Titans are 31st in the NFL in yards per play (4.5), last in points scored (58), 28th in quarterback rating (77.2), and 27th in rushing yards per game (82.6). Unless Indianapolis was without defensive lineman DeForest Buckner, cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, and most other good starters, Indianapolis should be able to outscore Tennessee easily. And Buckner, Ward, and Gardner are healthy and will play in Week 6. The Titans haven't beaten Indianapolis since October 2022, a stretch of six straight wins for the Colts, and Indy has no excuse for not making that seven straight victories at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday. Injuries won't be a problem for the Colts, at least heading into the game. Tennessee won't have starting safety Kevin Winston Jr., but otherwise they are mostly healthy. They just don't have a lot of talent. They haven't defeated any AFC South team since January 2024, and if that changes against the Colts in Week 6, Indianapolis needs to make some immediate changes. Ultimately, Sunday should be a get-healthy game for the Indianapolis Colts as far as record and standing in the division. When all else is going on, at least Indianapolis can count on two wins every season against the dismal Tennessee Titans . away.headline: Colts Could Be Without Key Offensive Weapon Against Titans
away.blurb: Several key players appear to be trending in the right direction, but Indianapolis has already ruled out two contributors, and rookie tight end Tyler Warren remains questionable. Through five games, he has 30 catches for 213 yards and two touchdowns, trailing only Josh Downs in receiving yards for Indianapolis. Losing him would be a massive blow to a passing attack that is already running out of healthy weapons. Alec Pierce remains on injured reserve, Darius Slayton was released Friday without ever appearing in a game for Indianapolis, and Dulin has now been ruled out for a second straight week. Will Mallory practiced fully all week as he works his way back from a thumb injury, although he is also listed as questionable while Indianapolis decides whether to activate him from injured reserve. Jonathan Taylor logged his second consecutive full practice, while Jalen Travis progressed from not practicing Wednesday to limited Thursday and full participation Friday. Grover Stewart returned to full participation after a rest day Thursday, while Charvarius Ward has now practiced fully on back-to-back days. DeForest Buckner did not practice Friday, but his absence was rest-related. Carlies being out for a second straight week still hurts a linebacker room that has struggled early this season, but Warren's status carries the biggest offensive implications. With an already depleted receiving corps, having Warren available could be the difference between an offense that finds its rhythm and another frustrating afternoon for Daniel Jones. Friday brought a mixed bag of injury news for the Indianapolis Colts ahead of Sunday's AFC South matchup with the Tennessee Titans. Of all the developments on Friday's report, Warren's status is easily the one that concerns me most. Tyler Warren Remains the Biggest Question Mark Warren was arguably the only bright spot for this offense in last week's 34-22 loss to Pittsburgh, catching seven passes for 83 yards and adding a one-yard rushing touchdown. That leaves Keenan Allen, Josh Downs, Laquon Treadwell and Deion Burks as the primary wide receiver options, with Warren's status potentially making things even thinner. Warren wasn't listed on the injury report Wednesday or Thursday, making his late-week appearance with a groin injury even more concerning. The good news is Allen and Downs have logged two straight full practices after lighter workloads Wednesday. Daniel Jones was also a full participant all three days despite remaining on the report with an ankle designation. Most of the Report Trended in the Right Direction Outside of Warren, Carlies and Dulin, Friday was fairly encouraging. Tennessee owns PFF's 26th-ranked coverage unit through five weeks, which should give Indianapolis an opportunity to attack through the air. But without Pierce, Dulin and potentially Warren, I am not sure the Colts have enough firepower to fully take advantage. That could put even more pressure on Downs and Taylor. home.headline: Colts' Week 6 injury report gives fans every reason to expect a Titans win
home.blurb: The Indianapolis Colts must feel pretty good about their health because they released Darius Slayton even though the team has struggled with wide receiver injuries this season. Not so much in Week 6, even though Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is going to be out and Alec Pierce still is . The positive is that Indy has a bye week, also known as having a matchup against the Tennessee Titans. As for Alec Pierce, no timeline exists for when he might return after reinjuring his heel. That might not happen until midseason, and the Colts will probably have far tougher games than the Titans before Pierce comes back. Besides Dulin, the only Indy player who will miss the game, according to head coach Shane Steichen , is linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs), but both Carlies and Dulin missed Week 5, and the reason the team lost to the Pittsburgh Steelers had nothing to do with the absences of Dulin and Carlies. The reason was that the defense was terrible again. Therein lies the difference between the Steelers and the Titans, as no matter how bad Indy's defense can be at times, Tennessee doesn't have the offensive talent that Pittsburgh has. Indianapolis Colts should be healthy enough to easily defeat the Tennessee Titans in Week 6 The Titans are 31st in the NFL in yards per play (4.5), last in points scored (58), 28th in quarterback rating (77.2), and 27th in rushing yards per game (82.6). Unless Indianapolis was without defensive lineman DeForest Buckner, cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, and most other good starters, Indianapolis should be able to outscore Tennessee easily. And Buckner, Ward, and Gardner are healthy and will play in Week 6. The Titans haven't beaten Indianapolis since October 2022, a stretch of six straight wins for the Colts, and Indy has no excuse for not making that seven straight victories at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday. Injuries won't be a problem for the Colts, at least heading into the game. Tennessee won't have starting safety Kevin Winston Jr., but otherwise they are mostly healthy. They just don't have a lot of talent. They haven't defeated any AFC South team since January 2024, and if that changes against the Colts in Week 6, Indianapolis needs to make some immediate changes. Ultimately, Sunday should be a get-healthy game for the Indianapolis Colts as far as record and standing in the division. When all else is going on, at least Indianapolis can count on two wins every season against the dismal Tennessee Titans . home.headline: Colts Could Be Without Key Offensive Weapon Against Titans
home.blurb: Several key players appear to be trending in the right direction, but Indianapolis has already ruled out two contributors, and rookie tight end Tyler Warren remains questionable. Through five games, he has 30 catches for 213 yards and two touchdowns, trailing only Josh Downs in receiving yards for Indianapolis. Losing him would be a massive blow to a passing attack that is already running out of healthy weapons. Alec Pierce remains on injured reserve, Darius Slayton was released Friday without ever appearing in a game for Indianapolis, and Dulin has now been ruled out for a second straight week. Will Mallory practiced fully all week as he works his way back from a thumb injury, although he is also listed as questionable while Indianapolis decides whether to activate him from injured reserve. Jonathan Taylor logged his second consecutive full practice, while Jalen Travis progressed from not practicing Wednesday to limited Thursday and full participation Friday. Grover Stewart returned to full participation after a rest day Thursday, while Charvarius Ward has now practiced fully on back-to-back days. DeForest Buckner did not practice Friday, but his absence was rest-related. Carlies being out for a second straight week still hurts a linebacker room that has struggled early this season, but Warren's status carries the biggest offensive implications. With an already depleted receiving corps, having Warren available could be the difference between an offense that finds its rhythm and another frustrating afternoon for Daniel Jones. Friday brought a mixed bag of injury news for the Indianapolis Colts ahead of Sunday's AFC South matchup with the Tennessee Titans. Of all the developments on Friday's report, Warren's status is easily the one that concerns me most. Tyler Warren Remains the Biggest Question Mark Warren was arguably the only bright spot for this offense in last week's 34-22 loss to Pittsburgh, catching seven passes for 83 yards and adding a one-yard rushing touchdown. That leaves Keenan Allen, Josh Downs, Laquon Treadwell and Deion Burks as the primary wide receiver options, with Warren's status potentially making things even thinner. Warren wasn't listed on the injury report Wednesday or Thursday, making his late-week appearance with a groin injury even more concerning. The good news is Allen and Downs have logged two straight full practices after lighter workloads Wednesday. Daniel Jones was also a full participant all three days despite remaining on the report with an ankle designation. Most of the Report Trended in the Right Direction Outside of Warren, Carlies and Dulin, Friday was fairly encouraging. Tennessee owns PFF's 26th-ranked coverage unit through five weeks, which should give Indianapolis an opportunity to attack through the air. But without Pierce, Dulin and potentially Warren, I am not sure the Colts have enough firepower to fully take advantage. That could put even more pressure on Downs and Taylor. home.headline: Germaine Pratt aiming to bring leadership, stability to defense in second go-around with Colts
home.blurb: The Colts are seeking consistency at linebacker, with snaps divided in Week 5 between Akeem Davis-Gaither (52 snaps), Austin Ajiake (32 snaps), CJ Allen (24 snaps) and Bryce Boettcher (11 snaps) with starting WILL linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs) out. As with Davis-Gaither, the Colts see value in Pratt's experience not only in the NFL, but with Anarumo's system. Germaine Pratt aiming to bring leadership, stability to defense in second go-around with Colts Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE The Colts signed the 30-year-old Pratt, who started 12 games for them in 2025, to their practice squad on Tuesday. While Germaine Pratt went unsigned up until Tuesday, he found a way to still be involved in football. The 30-year-old veteran linebacker spent time in the summer as a volunteer coach at North Carolina State , where he worked with his alma mater's linebackers. He eventually had a tryout with the Dallas Cowboys, though he didn't sign. This week, Pratt got his chance to get back into playing instead of coaching. The Colts signed him to their practice squad on Tuesday, and while it's too early to tell if and when he'll make his 2026 debut, Pratt said his goal is to use his experience to bring leadership to the Colts' linebacker room. "Helping the defense, just being in this system for so long, that's all I know," Pratt said. "So help it stabilize and settle it down, make tackles, whatever the case may be, get some turnovers." Pratt has played all but four of his 112 NFL games for Lou Anarumo, his defensive coordinator with the Cincinnati Bengals (2019-2024) and Colts (2025). In 2025, Pratt signed with the Colts in October after being released by the Las Vegas Raiders and started 12 games, totaling 101 tackles, a forced fumble and an interception. The experienced WILL linebacker has had over 100 tackles with at least one interception and one forced fumble every year since 2023. "Just adding a veteran presence is big in there," head coach Shane Steichen said. "He's played a lot of football in this league, made a lot of plays, and any time you can add good players to your roster, you want to do that." In the immediate future, whether Pratt could factor into that group on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans – he'd have to be elevated to the active roster from the practice squad – remains to be seen given he didn't participate in training camp and took the field for his first practice of the 2026 season on Wednesday. "I don't know the plan," Pratt said. The Dallas Cowboys entered Thursday night’s showdown with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as 9.5-point favorites, yet they lost outright at home, destroying plenty of Survivor entries in the process. Week 5 had three teams that were obvious Survivor selections: Dallas, Houston and Cincinnati. They were all playing 0-4 teams, but only the Bengals and Texans came through. Luckily for the SI Betting team, neither of our editors selected the Cowboys this week, meaning that if you tailed our picks , you’re still alive heading into Week 6. Bye weeks are really starting to come into play in Survivor, as the Detroit Lions, Minnesota Vikings, Miami Dolphins and Bengals all won’t play in Week 6. One of the best strategies in Survivor this season has been fading the 0-5 Dolphins, so players will have to look elsewhere on Sunday. There are still some huge favorites in Week 6, the Los Angeles Rams are favored by double digits at home against the Arizona Cardinals, and the Kansas City Chiefs, Indianapolis Colts and New England Patriots are all favored by at least a touchdown at home. Each week, the SI Betting team of Iain MacMillan and Peter Dewey makes their favorite Survivor selections each week to help guide our readers through the season. Here’s a recap of our Week 5 selections before we dive into our favorite Survivor teams in Week 6. NFL Week 5 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Cincinnati Bengals (W) Iain MacMillan: Houston Texans (W) Both Dewey and MacMillan faded winless teams in Week 5, and both wins were relatively sweat free with the Texans blowing out Tennessee and Cincy cruising to a big lead in a seven-point win over Miami. There are still plenty of playoff contenders that we can choose from in Week 6, even in just a 14-game slate. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 6 Survivor Pool Picks Indianapolis Colts Indianapolis is going to be a popular pick in Survivor this week because it’s playing the Titans, but I’m willing to take a shot on Daniel Jones and company to get back to .500 at 3-3, especially at home. Indy is currently a seven-point favorite against the worst team in the AFC South. Cam Ward and the Titans have been downright awful on offense, ranking dead last in yards per play, 31st in EPA/Play and 26th in success rate during their 0-5 start. They’ve scored 20 or fewer points in every game, including three games where they scored 10 or less points. Indianapolis hasn’t done a great job of finishing drives this season, but it has one of the best kickers in the NFL in Spencer Shrader. So, Indy is able to get enough points on the board (like it did in Week 5) even if it doesn’t score a bunch of touchdowns. The Colts are allowing the third-most yards per play in the NFL on defense, which is a concern for them when it comes to this pick. However, Tennessee is 2-8 on the road in the Ward era, and it has covered the spread in just four of those games. The Indy offense isn’t a juggernaut, but it has moved the ball a lot better than the Titans, hanging 30 points on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 2 while ranking 21st in success rate and 22nd in EPA/Play. I don’t see many spots where I’d willingly take the Colts in Survivor, so this is a way to use them and hopefully advance to Week 7. Indy at home against the Titans is by far the most favorable game on the team’s schedule outside of a Nov. 15 home game against Miami. The Titans have been lost to open this season, and I don’t expect them to turn things around any time soon with how abysmal their offense has looked. The Colts may not cover, but they should handle business at home in Week 6. – Peter Dewey New England Patriots The New England Patriots proved last week that they still can show flashes of the team that won the AFC last season, especially when they play the weaker teams in the NFL. picks.blurb: Latest Teams On Air Listen + Watch Contests Events More LISTEN LIVE Home The New York Jets will look to win their second consecutive game when they visit the New England Patriots at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday. Head coach Aaron Glenn’s team… Ezra Bernstein Updated Oct 16, 2026 2:41 PM EDT Pamela Smith/Getty Images Share this story The New York Jets will look to win their second consecutive game when they visit the New England Patriots at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday. Head coach Aaron Glenn's team has already exceeded expectations, staying competitive in every single one of its games this season while claiming a couple of victories against the Tennessee Titans and the Cleveland Browns. Meanwhile, the Patriots have rebounded from a slow start, rattling off two consecutive wins against the Buffalo Bills and the Las Vegas Raiders to round out a 3-2 record. Moving past another divisional opponent would keep New England in contention for the AFC East crown early in the season. As many expected coming into the campaign, the strength of this Jets team is its defense. Rookie defensive end David Bailey already has five sacks while four other players have two. New York is yet to force many turnovers, but the offense has been so good at limiting its own that it has not been much of a factor. The only giveaway that the Jets have on their stat sheet is a lost fumble from rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq, indicating a competent level of play from quarterback Geno Smith, who has managed every game adequately thus far. New England's defense will provide Smith with one of his biggest challenges of the season. Head coach Mike Vrabel's unit has forced six turnovers through five games, largely because of an excellent secondary led by cornerback Christian Gonzalez. It helps that defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr has created a scheme that consistently fools opposing passers, utilizing a variety of blitzes, rotations, and coverages to force offensive indecision on a snap-to-snap basis. With quarterback Drake Maye playing increasingly well, New England once again looks like a serious playoff contender in a crowded AFC.
