Drake Maye and the offense are finding their footing, and the Jets arrive after winning a game against the Browns that nobody needs to watch twice. New England's backfield takes a hit with TreVeyon Henderson expected to miss multiple weeks. More work for Rhamondre Stevenson, and another reason Maye needs to keep this passing game moving. Breece Hall's availability matters for New York. The Jets need sustained possessions, manageable third downs and a game that doesn't force them to chase points. I like the Patriots to control this one without needing another 45-point afternoon. Win the turnover battle and the rest should follow. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Patriots 31, Jets 17 In one of the sharpest early-season turnarounds we've seen thus far in 2026, Drake Maye is fully back to his NFL MVP runner-up form. That's a difficult blow for the Jets, who probably needed to face the more error-prone version of the quarterback in order to score an upset. Rookie David Bailey and the pass rush might give Gang Green a chance if they can keep Maye under pressure, but the defense's struggles to generate any takeaways cap the potential for chaos here. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Patriots 28, Jets 21 Everyone believes the Patriots are back. Are they? New England took advantage of a porous Bills defense and then an upstart Raiders bunch that had to travel across the country following a deflating defeat to the rival Chiefs. Credit the Patriots for taking care of business, but Drake Maye still has a long way to go before entering the circle of trust again. The Jets could get some reinforcements back this week and Aaron Glenn's defense has been respectable. The Patriots still get the job done, but it could be closer than some might expect. away.blurb: Both rookies fully practiced on Friday and appear ready to go. Sadiq was earlier listed as questionable with concussion symptoms, but apparently has passed the NFL protocols. Gang Green received some good news this week, as tight end threat Kenyon Sadiq appears likely to play after passing through the NFL concussion protocols. He will be a game-time decision but practiced fully on Thursday. Also expected to boost the Jets is the return from injured reserve of rookie Omar Cooper Jr. A No. 1 choice out of Indiana, Cooper went down with a high ankle sprain on opening day against the Tennessee Titans. In his brief playing time, though, he impressed with a 30-yard catch and run that scattered Titans defenders. The looming big question for the Patriots is whether star receiver A.J. Brown has recovered from an ankle injury. Brown was listed as limited on the injury report, a definition that likely means he won't be at full strength for Sunday's contest. Christian Gonzalez, the Patriots' top cornerback, practiced fully on Thursday after missing two games with a shoulder injury. If he plays on Sunday, he will draw a tough assignment: shut down the Jets' star receiver Garrett Wilson, who leads his team with 31 catches, 374 yards and three touchdowns. Wilson's stats are all the more impressive given that he's played most of the season without a true No. 2 receiver to take the heat off his coverage. If he can't go, No. 1 draft choice Caleb Lomu will take his place. He performed well as a sub in the Raiders game, going 29 snaps without allowing a sack. home.headline: Patriots Get A.J. Brown Update as 16-Player Injury Report Raises New Concerns
home.blurb: A.J. Brown , who had been on the injured reserve list after the Sept. 9 season opener against the Seahawks in Seattle, returned to Patriots practice Wednesday as a limited participant, opening a 21-day window that makes Sunday's Jets game his earliest possible, though not very likely, return. Brown's return arrives after quarterback Drake Maye threw for 374 yards and four touchdowns Sunday, leaving open whether Brown plays New York or waits for Chicago, according to The Boston Globe reporter Nicole Yang . Maye was also named on Wednesday's injury report with a right shoulder condition, though out of all 16 players only Maye was listed as a full participant in practice. “He hadn't been out there for four weeks, so we'll get him back out there practicing and see if he's ready to go in a couple days,” coach Mike Vrabel said, as quoted by CBS Sports . The Patriots play the New York Jets in Foxborough on Sunday, Oct. 18, then visit the Chicago Bears on Thursday night, Oct. 22. That gives Brown two possible return dates in five days. No quotes from Brown were available after the session. He was all smiles in the locker room beforehand, according to WEEI radio host Meghan Ottolini . None of the Wednesday reports mentioned a physical setback during practice. Brown has been “pushing to practice this week,” according to NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport , who also said a return against the Jets “may be a bit early to return from a high-ankle sprain.” Cornerbacks Carlton Davis III (neck) and Karon Prunty (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday, according to the injury report. Twelve other players were limited. They were tackles Marcus Bryant (ankle), Will Campbell (knee) and Morgan Moses (foot); safeties Byard (chest) and Craig Woodson (shoulder); linebackers Christian Elliss (chest) and Dre'Mont Jones (shoulder); cornerbacks Channing Canada (hamstring), Christian Gonzalez (shoulder), Marcus Jones (ankle) and Charles Woods (shoulder); and running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle). Maye, listed with a right shoulder issue, practiced fully. Patriots Get A.J. Brown Update as 16-Player Injury Report Raises New Concerns Unlock the latest Heavy on Patriots news — direct to your inbox. But the massive injury report contained at least one piece of good news for New England. Brown, slated to be the Patriots' No. 1 wide receiver, missed four games with a high ankle sprain suffered in the season-opening loss to Seattle. home.headline: Patriots week 6 injury report: AJ Brown returns, OTs banged up bad
home.blurb: "I mean, I think that we'll just focus on this week and see if guys are ready to go," Mike Vrabel said Wednesday about handling injuries ahead of this week and next week's Thursday Night Football game. "We obviously know we have a shortened week next week. It can’t impact our decisions to try to do everything we can to win this week. Then we’ll figure out where we are after that." The biggest story for the Patriots? The return of A.J. Brown, who missed Weeks 2 through 5 with a high-ankle sprain . He was designated to return off of IR this week, and will work to try and play this week against a Jets team he should thrive against. "He hasn't been out there, so I can't tell you until we actually see it," Vrabel said. "He hasn't been out there for four weeks, so we'll get him back out there practicing and see if he's ready to go in a couple days. And if not, then we have a 21-day window, and we'll go from there." Last week against the Raiders, the Patriots lost both TreVeyon Henderson and Will Campbell in a matter of minutes. Both players would leave the game and wouldn't return, and after tests on Monday, could end up missing some time . When reporters were present during Wednesday's practice, neither of them were spotted on the field with their teammates. Campbell did speak prior to going out to practice, but he only participated in a limited capacity. When Campbell was ruled out, the Patriots turned to first round rookie Caleb Lomu . He would play pretty good football from the left side — allowing just one pressure in 47 snaps. After starting the week as a limited participant, Christian Gonzalez was upgraded to a full participant for Thursday. He's been on the field working as a starter after missing the past two weeks of practice, and is now in line to make his return to the game field. Earlier this week, Gonzalez told reporters that he was "ready to go" for his battle with the Jets. Now that he's a full go in practice, the Patriots coaching staff is looking forward to seeing their top cornerback return to action. "He's the same guy," cornerbacks coach Justin Hamilton said. "He came back out and prepares, going to work, playing the game in his head like what he always has done." 3 Winners, 4 Losers of A.J. New England Patriots starting left tackle Will Campbell suffered a knee injury during this past Sunday's Week 5 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Campbell underwent MRI testing to determine the severity of his injury on Monday. And according to a report from NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the 22-year-old offensive lineman avoided a serious, long-term injury. Campbell is now considered "week-to-week" as the Patriots prepare for this coming Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the division-rival New York Jets. “We’ll see how the week goes,” Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said of Campbell's injury status on Monday. “It’ll get looked at and continues to rehab. The Giants tied with the Washington Commanders in what ended up being one of the weirder games of the season. New York should have lost to Washington, so the fact that they tied is being taken as a win for the team. But the Giants know that they will need a better effort going forward this week as the team gets ready to face off against the New Orleans Saints at home. New Orleans will be coming into the game looking to stop the bleeding, with the Saints sitting with a record of 1-4 on the year. Both sides need a win this week for different reasons, and the Giants will try to remain perfect at home this season. New York can't overlook this Saints team despite their struggles this season; otherwise, the Giants could find themselves in a tight contest. Bleacher Report did game predictions for every contest this week, with Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford picking. In these predictions, every single expert went with the Giants to take down New Orleans. Much of this could be due to the Saints having their own problems this year, but the Giants have shown real promise as a team. Even with starting quarterback Jaxson Dart going down with an injury, the Giants have been able to stay the course. Backup signal-caller Jameis Winston has held down the fort well for New York, showing that he can get this team to the playoffs. But the problem with Winston is that he has been very inconsistent over the years in his career, and the Giants know this from the first few weeks of the season. As he gets ready to face off against New Orleans, Winston will need to make sure to stay focused. Winston can be very turnover-prone at times, and the Giants can't afford any issues against the Saints this week. The Giants defense has been a calling card for the team this season, helping them win a few games. And going against an explosive Saints passing attack, the New York secondary will need to be ready to go. The kickoff for the game between the Giants and Saints is scheduled for 10:00 a.m. PT/1:00 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey

picks.headline: Saints Rookie Report: Week 6 preview vs. the Giants
picks.blurb: Saints Rookie Report: Week 6 preview vs. the Giants - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Saints Rookie Report: Week 6 preview vs. the Giants NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 11: Lorenzo Styles Jr. #36 of the New Orleans Saints plays against the Minnesota Vikings during the first half of a game at Caesars Superdome on October 11, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Caleb Yaccarino Wed, October 14, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads I want to start this week's report by talking about this class. Like many, I have seen it ranked very low on lists of the best and worst classes from 2026. I don't disagree with those lists, and really, who can? Injuries, players being behind veterans, or some still needing to develop have kept this class from doing much, but you shouldn't lose faith in this group. The players who have been in the game have made plays that are good starting points, and although development matters, it's not like those players have been bad. Jordyn Tyson's injury is annoying to say the least, but hopefully we can forget about that once he's back. Do I think this class is going to be like 2025? No, but in hindsight, I think he could be a nice, middle-of-the-road draft class. Now onto the players: DT Christen Miller Finally, Christen Miller was able to get into the game on Sunday, and eventhough the Saints could not win, he did well in his short time. Miller made big plays against the run, took up blocks from offensive linemen to open up holes for other defensive linemen and the linebackers to stop the run, and in my opinion, proved he should be the starting nose tackle. It wasn't perfect, but it was enough for the Saints to play him more. This should hopefully be the case against the New York Giants, and to stop RB Cam Skattebo, you need a big defensive lineman that can prevent him from carrying the pile. TE Oscar Delp With the Vikings sending blitzes nearly every play, Delp had to step up as a blocker, and he did. The Giants are also at the top of the league in blitz rate, so Delp will be a primary blocker once again. I do hope the Saints utilize him as a receiver, because Noah Fant has had pre-snap issues this season, and prioritizing youth should be the plan moving forward. Try something new. OG Jeremiah Wright Speaking of trying something new, I wish Jeremiah Wright would get some snaps, but now that pressure is on the organization to win, a Cesar Ruiz trade feels less likely due to the risk. If a coaching change is made, I hope the next staff will give Wright a chance. WR Bryce Lance Last week, I said that it's clear Lance is not ready for WR3, and the Vikings game only reinforced that. The Saints need to make the move and put him at WR4 moving forward so he can learn. I know I have said to prioritize youth, but I also want to prioritize Tyler Shough's development, and Lance is negatively affecting that. WR Barion Brown Brown is a similar spot to Lance, but it's also clear he needs to figure out the return game as well. His fellow former LSU Tiger, Zavion Thomas, is in nearly the exact same spot with the Bears, but due to their offensive struggles with Caleb Williams being out, they have begun to utilize Thomas more. In addition, Thomas has improved as their main return man. Hopefully, the same can happen for Brown. RB CJ Donaldson Donaldson was thrown to the wolves trying to block the Vikings blitz, and although I felt he did a decent job, he did have a holding call on one of the plays. As a rusher, Donaldson did exactly what I thought, picking up tough yards that did help the Saints in their run game. Against the Giants, I want him to be included once again. OT Mason Murphy In probably the most confusing moment of the game, which is saying a lot, the Saints put in Mason Murphy on a random drive, then subbed him out for Asim Richards the next. At first, I thought Richards got injured, but Moore said after the game that it was planned. I actually thought Richards did better than usual, and Murphy wasn't great when he came in. I don't think the Saints will make this substitution again. DB Lorenzo Styles Jr. Styles Jr. was back last game, which was nice to see, but his involvement was limited. I wouldn't be shocked if that changes after Jayden Price's release being cut, so Styles Jr. could be the return man next to Brown against the Giants. Injured players: WR Jordyn Tyson

Starting EDGE Abdul Carter (calf), starting right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and starting left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin) are all officially questionable to face the Saints. They were all limited Friday, giving them at least a chance to suit up. Starting cornerback Colton Hood (concussion) starting safety Tyler Nubin (neck) have been declared out, making the Giants secondary depleted. away.headline: Giants Injury Report: Six Players Get Game Designations Ahead of Saints
away.blurb: Tight end Theo Johnson (neck), safety Tyler Nubin (neck) and cornerback Colton Hood (concussion) have all been declared out for the contest. Johnson’s status is also worth monitoring in future weeks, given that he went from a limited participant on Wednesday and Thursday to being kept out of practice on Friday. Three key Giants are listed as questionable for Sunday: both starting offensive tackles, Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and Andrew Thomas (groin), and starting outside linebacker Abdul Carter (calf). All three were limited in practice Friday, an upgrade after they were held out Wednesday and Thursday. The feeling is that both tackles should be good to go for Sunday. If not, rookie J.C. Davis will get the nod at left tackle, where he played well in the preseason, and Marcus Mbow will start at right tackle. The assigned game participation statuses to six players on Friday ahead of their Week 6 home game against the New Orleans Saints. That is the most injury designations the Giants have had this season. Johnson’s absence means Thomas Fidone II, who has been a healthy scratch through the first four games of the season before finally getting a suit last week, will see a larger role on offense this Sunday. “Oh, he could help us. He could help us,” head coach John Harbaugh said of Fidone. “He’s had great practices, runs good routes, and played well on special teams last week. Thomas is ready to play, as he showed last week.” The Giants are getting safety Jason Pinnock back for the week after he missed last week due to a concussion. Pinnock appeared to have quietly passed Nubin on the depth chart for a starting job, but the concussion he suffered two weeks ago gave Nubin a mulligan last week. Carter’s status is also worth monitoring. He’s been a big part of the defensive pass rush. With the Giants already missing Brian Burns for the rest of the season due to an ACL injury, not having Carter would be a huge blow to a pass rush that has started to click over the last couple of weeks. home.headline: Saints vs. Giants: Jameis Winston's Return Headlines 3 Key Storylines
home.blurb: Saints Injury Report: Shough Limited, Kamara Sidelined Ahead of Vikings This article was originally published on www.si.com/nfl/saints/onsi as Saints vs. Giants: Jameis Winston's Return Headlines 3 Key Storylines . The New Orleans Saints enter Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the New York Giants looking to avoid their fourth consecutive loss, but a familiar face stands in their way and remains a fan favorite in New Orleans. Former Saints quarterback Jameis Winston will lead the Giants against his former team as New Orleans attempts to rebound from a disappointing 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings . The Saints (1-4) have struggled to find consistency on both sides of the football, particularly offensively, where turnovers and an ineffective passing attack have contributed to their disappointing start. Meanwhile, the Giants (3-1-1) have emerged as one of the NFC's early surprises under first-year coach John Harbaugh, overcoming injuries and inconsistent quarterback play to remain atop the NFC East. Beyond Winston's reunion with New Orleans, the Saints must contend with two dangerous receiving threats in Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely while finding a way to exploit New York's ball-security problems. Here are three major storylines to watch heading into Sunday's matchup. Winston, a fan favorite among Who Dat Nation, will be the starter against his former team. The former No. 1 overall pick spent four seasons with the Saints from 2020-23, initially serving as Drew Brees ' backup before becoming New Orleans' starting quarterback in 2021. Now, Winston has the chance to face his former team while trying to keep the Giants atop the NFC East. Winston became the starter after Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending injury. Through three starts this season, Winston has thrown for 805 yards, six touchdowns and three interceptions while completing 57.6% of his passes. In his latest outing against Washington, Winston helped engineer the comeback by completing 33 of his 54 passes for 326 yards and three touchdowns, connecting twice with Isaiah Likely and once with Malik Nabers . Perhaps most importantly, Winston avoided throwing an interception despite attempting 54 passes. Can the Saints Slow Down Malik Nabers and Isiah Likely? While Winston commands attention, the Saints' biggest defensive challenge may be containing his top targets, wide receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely. Nabers (29 catches for 329 yards and two touchdowns) and Likely (33 catches for 284 yards and four touchdowns) are responsible for 58% of the yardage production and number of targets thrown to. Nabers, a former LSU star, has bounced back from a season-ending knee injury. He caught six passes for 112 yards and a touchdown against Arizona in Week 4, then recorded 11 catches for 121 yards and a touchdown on 20 targets against Washington. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 6 schedule, including five locks against the spread Getty Images I don't know what it is about the Week 6 slate, but I think we're going to have some underdogs bark rather loudly. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. They're coming off a brilliant upset win over the Detroit Lions, too. The Philadelphia Eagles made the long trek back from London after a mindboggling, crushing defeat where victory was essentially secured. The Panthers have the advantage this week, it seems. Despite that, they're not favored on the road, and some experts aren't willing to pick the Panthers to take the Eagles down. Expert picks for Eagles vs. Panthers in NFL Week 6 action Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni reacts during the first half | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect CBS Sports' Pete Prisco has picked against the Panthers all season, his seeming disdain for the franchise refusing to go away. He isn't changing his ways this week, either, picking the Eagles to win by three despite giving ample reason the Panthers should win. CBS Sports' Pete Prisco has picked against the Panthers all season, his seeming disdain for the franchise refusing to go away. He isn't changing his ways this week, either, picking the Eagles to win by three despite giving ample reason the Panthers should win. "The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense," he wrote. His CBS colleague, Jordan Dajani, disagreed, picking the Panthers to win 23-21. "The Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS," Dajani pointed out. Here's how SI's staff is picking the game: Albert Breer: Panthers Eva Geitheim: Panthers Mitch Goldich: Eagles Mike Kadlick: Panthers Gilberto Manzano: Panthers Conor Orr: Eagles John Pluym: Eagles Matt Verderame: Eagles Bleacher Report's Wes O'Donnell is taking the Panthers to cover the spread and win outright. "I'm done trying to figure out the Eagles. The Eagles clearly cannot figure out the Eagles. And while the Panthers' defense is a great opportunity for any offense to get right, Carolina had a bye week and then some to prepare for Philly. This Panthers team has defied the odds and shown up in tough situations since last season," he wrote. Carolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales reacts after the game at Bank of America Stadium | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect His colleagues Gary Davenport, Kristopher Knox, Moe Moton, and Brent Sobleski agree, while Ian Hanford and Brad Gagnon disagree, picking the Eagles. His colleagues Gary Davenport, Kristopher Knox, Moe Moton, and Brent Sobleski agree, while Ian Hanford and Brad Gagnon disagree, picking the Eagles. At ESPN , only Pam Maldonado and Dan Graziano picked the Eagles to beat the Panthers. The Athletic's Vic Tafur was obscenely blunt: "The Eagles are coming off two heartbreaking losses, they struggle against play-action passes (a Panthers staple), and it wouldn’t shock me if this is Sirianni’s last game as head coach." What does this mean? Despite the overwhelming advantages the Panthers have in this game, there's still a perception that the Eagles are the Eagles and the Panthers are the woeful Panthers. That makes Week 6's contest a perfect opportunity to reshape the narrative, although it's a little unfair that a primetime victory over the Detroit Lions didn't do that for the Panthers. picks.blurb: Eagles-Panthers Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 6 enemy - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Eagles-Panthers Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 6 enemy PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - DECEMBER 08: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers throws a pass as Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles dives toward him in the first quarter of a game at Lincoln Financial Field on December 08, 2024 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brandon Lee Gowton Fri, October 16, 2026 at 3:55 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Philadelphia Eagles are returning to Lincoln Financial Field this weekend to host the Carolina Panthers. The Birds will be coming off a trip from London while their opponent is coming off a bye week. In order to preview this Week 6 matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Cat Scratch Reader . The witty Walker Clement kindly took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let's take a look at the answers. 1) Bryce Young seems to be playing well; three of his top seven games in terms of passer rating have taken place this season. How real is his improvement and what can it be attributed to? I'm scared to say it's real but that's mostly because we've been hurt before. Young was excusably atrocious (coaching dumpster fire) in his rookie year. He was worse to start his second season to the point that he got benched until an Andy Dalton broken thumb returned him to the line up. He was better, but not good. Last year, his third season, had ups and downs. The ups showed he was physically capable of playing well, a legitimate question up to that point. The downs proved he couldn't (yet) play well consistently. This season he seems to be playing well consistently. His worst game was against the Cleveland Browns when he had a mild, nagging knee injury that has apparently persisted through the bye week. Otherwise he has been one of the best quarterbacks in the league. His statistical improvement alone has been so stellar that he remained a top 10 passing quarterback through Week 5 despite having a bye in Week 5. So, is it real? Why is it real? I truly don't know but all of Panthers nation is what I would describe as cautiously giddy at this unexpected and welcome turnabout in Young's fortunes. We're also all fully braced for when the other shoe drops and knocks the wheels off of our clown car. 2 – Sounds like the Panthers could be getting some key players back for this game. Who are you expecting to return and what's the impact? What about the absences that Carolina could be dealing with? There are three players who could return to the lineup and have a significant impact over what the team put together against the Lions in their last game. First is Taylor Moton. He has started nearly every game for the Panthers at right tackle since 2018. He is an excellent player who will elevate the Panthers struggling run game if he is ready to play. There is no guarantee he will be up to the task after recovering from blood clots in his lungs during the offseason. But with back up and rookie right tackle Monroe Freeling questionable-at-best with a knee injury, the Panthers need every man they can find. Similarly, Tershawn Wharton may be ready to step into the ailing defensive line rotation. He should provide some much needed fresh legs and pass rushing acumen. Don't expect him to get a sack if he plays, but he should be contributing to pressure. The second most important returning player is wide receiver Jalen Coker. He is an incredibly talented guy and shares great chemistry with Bryce Young. He is a large part of Young's statistical improvement this year. With him on the field, McMillan shouldn't need to catch another 14 passes for 192 yards in a single game. 3 – The Eagles' offense stinks but the Panthers haven't exactly been one of the top defenses in the league. What are the strengths and weaknesses of that unit? The strengths entering Week 4 were the interior defensive line and the cornerbacks. Since then, defensive tackle Cam Jackson and cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson have landed on IR. Young corners Akayleb Evans and Will Lee III had rough outings against the Lions. Lee has promise, but he's a rookie who is still adjusting to the speed of the game. They are expected to start again this week. That leaves Devin Lloyd, who has been amazing, and Jaelan Phillips, who is a one-man show thanks to injuries across the rest of the front seven, as the noticeable strengths of the defense. It sounds bleak, but they managed to hold Jahmyr Gibbs to 46 yards on 15 carries in their last game. Anything can happen. 4 – What's the biggest matchup in the Panthers' favor and the biggest matchup against their favor? Wide receiver Tetarioa McMillan, the Week 4 NFC offensive player of the Week, vs anybody you have is the biggest match up in favor of the Panthers. Conversely, DeVonta Smith versus anybody left standing in a Panthers uniform after the snap is a huge mismatch against Carolina. That suggests an explosive, high scoring game with lots of fast scores. Right? 5 – Who wins this game and why? With the Eagles currently listed as 1.5-point home favorites, what's your score prediction? It a little bit depends on who they get back from injury, but I think these are two teams trending in opposite directions. The Panthers should ultimately win this one, but the idea of a shoot out decided by the performance of two star wide receivers will be wrong. I expect the Panthers to flip, or fumble, the script and end up narrowly winning a surprisingly defensive battle 17 – 14. I'd be comfortable widening the margin of victory if Young, Coker, and Moton are all fully cleared to play. I also wouldn't be surprised to see them look completely new to the game of football and lose by three possessions or more. Such is the confidence bred by our recent years of, uh, success.

picks.blurb: Analyst Predicts Steelers to Dominate Buccaneers in Week 6 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Analyst Predicts Steelers to Dominate Buccaneers in Week 6 Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers in a game against the Indianapolis Colts on Oct. 11, 2026 -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Aaron Becker Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:38 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads A NFL analyst is all in on the Pittsburgh Steelers for Week 6. The Pittsburgh Steelers are currently 2.5-point favorites for their Week 6 road game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. However, NFL analyst Conor Orr thinks the oddsmakers have it completely wrong. Orr predicts the Steelers will continue their hot streak and dominate the Buccaneers in Week 6. "I wanna see the Steelers go down to Tampa Bay and win another one of these games," Orr said . "I think they can win this game by three touchdowns." Orr has done a complete 180 in just a matter of a week. Heading into Week 5, he begged the Indianapolis Colts to put the Steelers out of their misery. "Clearly you have communication issues. Your coach came out and said your house is dirty and you need to clean your house. Something's a mess here," Orr said on the Heed the Call NFL Podcast . "I'm sick of [Aaron Rodgers]. I'm sick of watching this team. I'm sick of the receivers dropping balls. I'm sick of them having played one good game against the Bengals so we've got to take them seriously for another three weeks. Come on, Jonathan Taylor. Put up 400 yards and put his old, dying horse out of its misery and off my screen." However, after watching the Steelers offense come alive in their latest win, Orr issued an apology to the team and now seems to be a big believer in Pittsburgh. "I have totally done a 180, and I'll admit it, on this Steelers offense," Orr continued. "Down so many people, and even down to Ben Skowronek, this team has been able to find a way to manufacture points. Aaron Rodgers will have bad Rodgers games, but I've totally flipped on this." The Steelers do seem to have some new found life. Rodgers is playing very well and running back Jaylen Warren has been on another level, recording 176, 126 and 188-yard performances the past three weeks. The only question that remains is: Can the Steelers offense continue this type of production the rest of the season? picks.headline: Buccaneers, Steelers: Week 6 game preview
picks.blurb: Buccaneers, Steelers: Week 6 game preview - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Buccaneers, Steelers: Week 6 game preview Aug 16, 2025; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving (7) catches a touchdown pass in front of Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Payton Wilson (41) during the first quarter at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Will Walsh Thu, October 15, 2026 at 5:44 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Week 6 is set to be rolling into living rooms all throughout the nation and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are no longer winless. Todd Bowles and his pewter pirates managed to pull out a sensationally shocking upset of the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football. Behind the mighty galloping of Bucky Irving and the poise of UDFA Jalen Daniels, Tampa's marauders took over AT&T Stadium. This Sunday (for the third week in a row), it'll be another classic blueblood NFL franchise on the schedule for the Buccaneers— The Pittsburgh Steelers. "The offense can't score if they don't have the ball." How can the Buccaneers win? ARLINGTON, TX - OCTOBER 08: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers runs the ball during an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on October 8, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Bucs need to make sure they stay on schedule and stick to their gameplan. There are NFL teams that have the benefit of being able to get into different types of games and win in a variety of ways— The Buccaneers are not that team. If a win is in the cards, they need to make sure they are playing the hand that best suits them. Last week, in Dallas, Tampa did a phenomenal job of staying in the realm of football that they themselves are comfortable playing. The Buccaneers kept the ball on the ground, dominated time of possession— Starting with a 10-minute opening drive, and kept Dallas off-kilter. That dictation was not only an advantage for Tampa Bay, it's the reason they won. That in turn made the Cowboys play the game the Buccaneers needed to play, not the one Dallas wanted to play. It would be easy to say, 'If Bucky Irving rushes for nearly 200 yards, the Buccaneers have a good chance of winning' , but it's more than the yards on the stat sheet. Irving's performance was eye-popping, but it was the offense's ability to stay on the field that won Tampa Bay the game. The Buccaneers finished the game with just shy of 40 minutes time of possession, while Dallas' heralded offense held the ball for just 20. That discrepancy is catastrophic for any team to be on the wrong side of— Personified through the consistent cutaways by Amazon's broadcast as they kept showing defeated, disengaged, and dispirited Dallas Cowboys on the sideline. Consecutive weeks with 40 minutes of possession may not be on the docket, however, will the Buccaneers' offense be able to keep themselves steady, avoid turnovers, and push Pittsburgh to play the type of game Tampa wants to play? "The question isn't who is going to let me; it's who is going to stop me." How can the Buccaneers lose? The Steelers have had some inconsistent offense this year, but they've had 24-plus points in each of the last three weeks (30, 24, 34). Of course, they can't score if they don't play (See the above portion of this article). The Buccaneers' second best option for keeping Pittsburgh's points down, besides pilfering clock, is turnovers. Tampa's turnover differential on the season is not glamourous (-2). Maybe even more absurd, that hideous -2 sits boldly after the Bucs just had a +3 in their last contest. Aside from points themselves, nothing has ever been, or will ever be, a more clear determinant of wins and losses than turnovers. Teams that take the ball away win a lot more than teams that lose the ball. Having the ball means having more chances to score, more chances to score means more better odds you will score; ergo, turnovers are good. More importantly, for a struggling, very one-dimensional team like the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, turnovers level the playing field. The scenario is two-fold. Not only does it fall on your defense to force them, but your offense must avoid turnovers like a coach on the hot seat must avoid losing. Last week, Tampa hit the trifecta— Their defense (and special teams) took the ball away from Dallas three times. Jalen Daniels and the Bucs' offense did not turn the ball over at all and their coach on the heat seat avoided a loss. This week, it's not Dak Prescott it's Aaron Rodgers. Aaron Rodgers is a historically anti-turnover prone quarterback. The former Packers' legend, Jets' bust, and current Steelers' stopgap, has quite literally the greatest touchdown to interception ratio in NFL history— As in, number one. Rodgers is not the type of quarterback that you want to face if the gameplan is get the ball— however , against all odds, Tampa Bay's ever assailed head coach Todd Bowles has actually had a healthy level of success against Rodgers during his Bucs' tenure. The two haven't matched up since Rodgers left Green Bay, but the duels have actually largely favored Bowles. In three games versus Todd Bowles' Tampa Bay defense, Rodgers has a losing record and has looked extremely ordinary. The four-time NFL MVP has wracked up just five touchdowns and he's also tossed four interceptions. The backdrop is laid out much differently for the 2026 edition, Rodgers has a new team, a new (his old) coach, is playing at a completely different level (which may actually further favor Bowles), and Bowles does not have nearly the same defensive firepower he once did. Sunday, will likely be the last time the two battle— A final chapter in the story. The storylines for Sunday's Bowles-Rodgers epilogue, can Todd Bowles get him again? Rodgers has yet to play a clean game against Bowles' Bucs. Will the Buccaneers' offense be able to stay mistake free for a second straight week? Turnovers, like they had against Rodgers' former team two weeks ago, will almost assuredly sink them into a self-dug 1-5 hole.

away.headline: Steelers WR Depth Gets Even Worse With DK Metcalf News
away.blurb: On their final injury report ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, DK Metcalf was listed as questionable to play with an illness. Pittsburgh is already down three receivers for its bout with Tampa Bay. Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) was placed on the reserve/injured list, meaning the earliest he can return after missing the minimum of four games while on IR is in Week 10 following the team's Week 9 bye. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have also been ruled out vs. the Buccaneers after suffering their respective injuries in the first half of the Steelers' Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts. The Pittsburgh Steelers were delivered another potential blow at wide receiver. Though it's an illness rather than an injury, which is positive news long-term for the Steelers, it's yet another instance of a receiver dealing with some type of hinderance. Metcalf was not listed on either of the first two injury reports of the week before registering as a non-participant on October 16. On the season so far, he has recorded 225 yards and a touchdown across 19 receptions. Now, Pittsburgh will take a wait-and-see approach with Metcalf before kicking off against Tampa Bay and hope that it doesn't lose another receiver for that contest. away.headline: Steelers have perfect trade candidate as NFL quarterback injuries pile up
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: When it comes to potential trade landing spots for Rudolph, there are quite a few interesting options. The Philadelphia Eagles , for example, are dealing with a major quarterback controversy as Jalen Hurts recovers from a serious blood clot. The Los Angeles Chargers just placed their top backup quarterback, Trey Lance, on injured reserve with a groin injury. The Washington Commanders, although they saw starter Jayden Daniels return to action, unfortunately had Marcus Mariota go down with a right knee MCL sprain. Rudolph is an important backup for Pittsburgh's offense, but his value beyond 2026 takes a nosedive. The Steelers would be wise to capitalize on the multiple quarterback injuries plaguing the rest of the league and get whatever they can in return for Rudolph. With the NFL trade deadline less than a month away, the Pittsburgh Steelers may have a few big decision to make before the important date. This is especially true when it comes to quarterback Mason Rudolph, who may be more valuable as a trade asset for Pittsburgh. The Steelers are swimming in quarterbacks at the moment, with two veterans and two young quarterbacks hoping to become future starters in the league. It's fair to assume that Aaron Rodgers isn't going anywhere, nor are the young options in Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar. Rudolph, on the other hand, could be enticing to other quarterback-needy teams around the league. Rudolph should easily be viewed as one of the top backup options at quarterback, appearing in 36 games and making 19 starts, as well as holding a 9-9-1 career record. He's also thrown for 4,925 yards and 30 touchdowns, in addition to having experience in multiple offensive systems. away.headline: Steelers injury report: Pittsburgh enters road trip with abundance of injuries
away.blurb: Out of the bye, road trips to face the division rival Bengals and in-state rival Eagles await. Neither is a long trip in terms of mileage, but the Steelers have not won in Philadelphia since 1965, and it follows an AFC North dogfight. The receivers room is the most pressing problem. Pittman will be out for at least the next three games after being placed on injured reserve. The veteran was a key offseason acquisition but has only played in three games in which he’s caught seven passes for 89 yards. The extent of the injuries to Wilson and Skowronek, sustained against Indianapolis, are not yet known, but McCarthy said Monday that both will be out for at least the Tampa Bay game. The secondary is a bit better off. Ramsey spent the week leading up to the Colts game on the injury report but handled a normal workload. Only Dean was absent, and the Steelers have not yet taken the step of adding the free agent cornerback signing to injured reserve. Dean was a limited practice participant Wednesday while Ramsey was out with a wrist injury listed. McCarthy hinted strongly that Dowdle is expected back this week from the toe injury he sustained in Week 2 against New England. He was also limited Wednesday. That should help the offense manage the reps of Jaylen Warren, who’s handled a heavy workload in Dowdle’s absence. First-year coach Mike McCarthy’s team will play four of its next five games on the road starting this week, and it will take multiple longer – and daunting – trips to do so before things begin to moderate in the back half of the 2026 schedule. All of it will unfold amid mounting absences. Running back Rico Dowdle; receivers Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek; and defensive backs Jamel Dean and Jalen Ramsey have all been hurt in some form or fashion recently. The stretch will be one of, if not the, most grueling in the franchise’s history and could determine whether the Steelers ’ 3-2 start has legs, or whether another mediocre year awaits a franchise that hasn’t won an NFL playoff game since 2017. NFL Week 6 brings a road trip to Tampa Bay to face the Buccaneers . That’s a 1,000-or-so-mile trip right off the bat against a desperate 1-4 team that needs a win to preserve any postseason hopes. One week later, the Steelers will board a long flight to Paris to face the New Orleans Saints in the first NFL regular season game in France. It will be only the second international game for Pittsburgh since 2013. Vasquez Stephan Stroud Thu, October 15, 2026 at 8:20 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Rams welcome the Arizona Cardinals to SoFi Stadium on Sunday for an important NFC West matchup between two teams looking to improve their position in the division. Los Angeles enters the game at 2-3 after a heartbreaking 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday night. Arizona is 1-4 and coming off a disappointing 45-21 defeat against the Detroit Lions. Both teams need a strong performance, making Sunday's divisional matchup an important opportunity to build momentum. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:05 p.m. ET on FOX at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. Matthew Stafford Leads the Rams Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford will be a major factor in Sunday's game as Los Angeles looks to rebound from its difficult loss to Buffalo. Stafford has thrown for 1,572 yards and nine touchdowns through five games, establishing himself as the centerpiece of an offense capable of producing explosive plays. However, six interceptions have created problems, and protecting the football will be important against Arizona. Head coach Sean McVay will look to get the offense back on track by utilizing his talented group of playmakers. Wide receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams give Stafford two dangerous options in the passing game, while running back Kyren Williams provides balance on the ground. Williams has recorded 343 rushing yards and four rushing touchdowns, making him an important part of Los Angeles' offensive attack. The Rams will also need to adjust along the offensive line, with left tackle Alaric Jackson suspended for Sunday's matchup. Jacoby Brissett Looks to Keep Arizona Competitive Arizona quarterback Jacoby Brissett will lead the Cardinals as they attempt to bounce back from their loss to Detroit. Brissett has thrown for 1,110 yards and nine touchdowns this season. Despite Arizona's struggles, he has shown the ability to move the football through the air and keep the offense competitive. Tight end Trey McBride remains one of his most reliable targets, entering the matchup with 42 receptions for 308 yards and three touchdowns. Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love has also contributed to Arizona's offense, although his availability and workload will be worth monitoring after he missed practice Wednesday with an ankle issue. First-year head coach Mike LaFleur will need his offense to produce consistently against a Rams defense looking to force turnovers and create pressure. A Crucial NFC West Matchup Sunday's game gives Los Angeles an opportunity to recover from its overtime defeat and improve its record. Arizona needs a stronger defensive performance after allowing 45 points against Detroit. With Stafford leading an explosive passing attack and Brissett looking to keep the Cardinals competitive, both quarterbacks will face important challenges. The Rams and Cardinals have plenty to prove, and Sunday's matchup could be an important moment for both teams as the NFC West race continues.

picks.blurb: Opening lines: Spread: Rams -13.5 Moneyline: Rams -750; Cardinals +13.5 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Rams vs Cardinals expert picks Adam Kaufman: Rams 34, Cardinals 20 The Rams need a get-right game. Conveniently, the Cardinals are coming to town. Los Angeles has spent enough time trading punches with contenders. Now Matthew Stafford gets an Arizona defense that should provide a much friendlier afternoon, even with the shortened turnaround after Monday night. The Cardinals can move the ball through Trey McBride and Michael Wilson, and Jeremiyah Love gives the offense a reason to stay patient. I just don't see enough defensive resistance to keep the Rams from eventually creating separation, especially after the way they fell to the Bills . The concern is asking Los Angeles to cover a huge number after an overtime game. Winning this matchup feels considerably more straightforward. Give me Stafford, Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, Kyren Williams and enough explosive plays to put the Rams back in the win column. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Rams 38, Cardinals 20 Watch out, Arizona. The Rams might take out the frustrations of a 2-3 start on their divisional foe. The Cardinals haven't proven nearly capable of offering any resistance to an attack with as much firepower as Los Angeles, let alone stopping one. Maybe this isn't the game in which Carson Beck will make his NFL debut for Arizona as he looks to take on a role as more than a mere emergency quarterback, but a blowout might bring that possibility closer to reality. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Rams 31, Cardinals 16 Perhaps the Rams aren't the super team that we thought. A 2-3 start to the season certainly isn't doing the team any favors. However, Matthew Stafford looked like a quarterback that started to find himself again in Week 5 against the Bills. The Cardinals are the get-right team for every NFC West team that feels down about themselves. That's just the reality of being the doormat in a loaded division. Sean McVay's crew takes out all their frustrations on the lowly Cardinals, winning by a big margin to cover up all the special teams mistakes. away.headline: Rams-Cardinals injury report: Surprises for both teams on Friday
away.blurb: Additionally, Trent McDuffie and Kam Curl both got injured in practice on Thursday, raising some questions about their availability. Sean McVay said Friday that he's "feeling good about" Curl despite his questionable tag, and also believes Davis Allen is "trending in the right direction" with his foot injury. Allen doesn't have an injury designation, which means he's good to go against Arizona. McDuffie and Curl are questionable, making them the only players with game statuses for Sunday. The Cardinals already ruled out Jeremiyah Love due to an ankle injury, which leaves them without a top playmaker at running back. Tyler Allgeier will step up in Love's place, but he's not the dynamic runner and receiver that Love is. Budda Baker picked up a groin injury and did not practice on Friday, leading to a questionable tag for the Cardinals' star safety. Three others are questionable, including linebacker Zaven Collins. He missed Friday's practice with a hip injury. The Los Angeles Rams and Arizona Cardinals will play their first of two games this season on Sunday when they square off at SoFi Stadium. They both come into this contest a bit banged up, with the Cardinals missing one of their top playmakers on offense and the Rams still missing Myles Garrett. The Arizona Cardinals will be without one of their most promising young offensive players when they face the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. The decision comes after Love missed practice throughout the week while dealing with an injury that has affected his performance in recent games. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur confirmed Friday that Love would not play, emphasizing the importance of allowing the rookie time to recover. Love previously suffered a right ankle injury during the preseason, but that issue has since healed. His current injury involves his left ankle, which has bothered him for several weeks. The former Notre Dame standout has struggled to find consistency during his first NFL season, rushing for 245 yards and one touchdown through five games. His latest performance highlighted some of those difficulties. During Arizona's loss to the Detroit Lions last weekend, Love managed just 22 rushing yards on 12 carries. LaFleur acknowledged earlier this week that the injury has affected Love's ability to make the explosive cuts that helped establish him as one of college football's most dynamic running backs. away.headline: Arizona Cardinals injury report: Jeremiyah Love sits Wednesday
away.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals opened their practice week Wednesday for Sunday’s road game against the Los Angeles Rams and released their first injury report of Week 5. Running back Jeremiyah Love did not practice. It appeared that LaFleur claimed Williams would be unavailable for Sunday’s game when he said, “He’s not going to clear the concussion protocol.” The report is an estimate because the Rams did not practice after playing the Buffalo Bills Monday night. Recovered from the right high-ankle sprain suffered in the Aug. 13 preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders , his left ankle has been an issue for several weeks. He has felt good heading into games, but then aggravation occurs on the field. Head coach Mike LaFleur said, “Want to get this ankle right and do it the right way. He’s a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. Imagine being a running back in the NFL, trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you’re capable of. We all are in agreeance, as much as he wants to battle through, we’re all in agreeance right now that (he needs to) give a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on what that’ll entail for Sunday.” Asked about concern about it continuing to be a problem going forward, LaFleur said, “It’s an ankle, so you don’t know. I’m not a doctor and each body is a little bit different. The way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable. He doesn’t even feel it, but this one is the one that happened when the regular season started and it’s just lingering.” The full details their Wednesday injury repory are below. home.headline: Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams
home.blurb: TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals are holding star rookie running back Jeremiyah Love out of practice on Wednesday as Week 6 preperations for the Los Angeles Rams ramp up. Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams Skip to main content SI.COM "Take him one day at a time. You know, we want to get this ankle right and do it the right way," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday. Love has been nursing an ankle injury through the opening stages of his rookie season after suffering a different ankle injury during preseason. While he hasn't missed any regular season action, Love's participation and impact has been slightly hindered. There's been some talks about potentially shutting Love down to allow the ankle to heal, though LaFleur didn't seem willing to do that. Arizona is just 1-4 and is again favored to lose in Los Angeles. "Listen, I'm going to try to be as candid as possible with also knowing that everyone's listening to this too, right? But he's a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. I mean, imagine being a running back in the NFL trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you know that you're capable of," LaFleur said. "And so we all are in agreeance — as much as you know he wants to battle through — we're all in agreeance right now, it's just hey, give [the injury] a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on, what that'll entail for Sunday." Love, the No. 3 overall pick, has 67 carries for 245 yards and one touchdown on the ground while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and a score through the air. "I think early at his career [he battled injuries], but you had the right [ankle] early, and then now you got the left one. So now you're just kind of — it's just double dipping. The right side, the preseason one's fine. It's the other one right now that's the lingering issue. They're ankles, you know, it's an ankle. I'm not a doctor, and each body's a little bit different," LaFleur continued. "Like the way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable, like he doesn't even feel it. But this one is the one that happened kind of when the regular season started, and it just lingered." Has Love lost any of his explosiveness? "You'd have to ask him that," LaFleur added. "I know how explosive he is. I know how explosive he wants to be. So I mean I think that's a fair assessment in some aspects. Again, I don't think it's an overall hindrance, but again the the rest for him is going to be vital." home.headline: Rams Injury Report Brings Much-Needed Good News Ahead of Week 6 vs. Cardinals
home.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams are set to enter Week 6 the healthiest they've been in weeks ahead of their matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. While the Rams didn't practice on Wednesday, each player's status is an estimation. On the injury report Rams had only one player who was estimated to not participate. That player was tight end Davis Allen, who would have missed practice with a foot injury. Outside of Allen, the Rams only had five other players listed, with four of them limited. While Allen is the only player who was estimated as a non-participant, linebacker Nate Landman (wrist/shoulder), wide receiver Alex Bachman (wrist), tight end Colby Parkinson (shoulder), and cornerback Josh Wallace (shoulder) were all limited. Both Landman and Parkinson have been on the injury report over the last few weeks as they manage various injuries. The Rams have managed Landman during the week before the last few games and will likely do the same with Parkinson. Arizona had multiple players who did not practice Wednesday due to rest. However, safety Wydett Williams didn't participate as he goes through the concussion protocol. Additionally, safety Kitan Crawford and wide receiver Devin Duvernay were both limited. There are still a few situations to monitor throughout the week on the Rams' side, particularly at tight end with Allen and Parkinson. However, compared to where things stood over the previous few weeks, they are in a much better position from a health standpoint. With the Rams looking to get back to .500 against the Cardinals, having most of their key contributors available should give them every opportunity to do just that. Kansas City is 4-0 after its bye, while Los Angeles is 0-5 following a 23-17 loss to Denver. Kickoff at Arrowhead Stadium is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. The Chiefs are favored by 8.5 points, but a routine favorite winning comfortably would hardly qualify as a bold prediction. Instead, this forecast projects an exceptional rushing performance, an unexpected Chargers defensive highlight and a fourth-quarter rally that changes the complexion of the afternoon without changing the winner. Kenneth Walker III rushes for 200 yards and three touchdowns Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Walker has already accumulated 537 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 87 carries through four games. That translates to more than six yards per attempt, giving Kansas City a foundation for dominating without asking Patrick Mahomes to carry every possession. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Chiefs average 6.5 yards per offensive play compared with the Chargers' 4.8. Their third-down conversion rate is also substantially better: 44% against 34.85%. Those advantages can sustain drives and produce the repeated rushing opportunities necessary for a monster individual afternoon. The prediction goes beyond another efficient outing. Walker reaches 200 rushing yards for the game and scores three times, becoming the central reason Kansas City controls possession and repeatedly finishes drives. There is an important limitation: Los Angeles allows only 5.0 yards per play, the same figure as Kansas City. This is not a forecast built on pretending the Chargers cannot defend. It depends on Walker maintaining his explosiveness while the Chiefs create an unusually favorable game script. If Kansas City builds an early advantage, sustained rushing volume can turn Walker's strong start into the biggest performance of his season. The Chargers intercept Patrick Mahomes twice, including a pick-six Mahomes has thrown nine touchdown passes against two interceptions through four games, with a 106.2 passer rating. Predicting two interceptions in one afternoon means Los Angeles matches his entire season total, despite entering winless. The statistical route to that surprise exists. The Chargers allow opponents to convert just 31.25% of third downs, compared with Kansas City's 37.04%. Forcing longer, obvious passing situations could provide opportunities that disappear when Walker keeps the offense ahead of schedule. Los Angeles needs more than ordinary defensive stops because its offense averages just 16.8 points per game. A defensive touchdown would change both field position and scoreboard pressure without requiring Justin Herbert to repeatedly rescue stalled possessions. The call is that one aggressive coverage read becomes an interception return for a touchdown, while another takeaway interrupts a promising Chiefs drive. That would be an unexpected blemish on Mahomes' efficient opening month. It would also illustrate why a team's record does not eliminate its capacity to produce a game-changing individual moment. Justin Herbert leads a 17-point fourth quarter, but Kansas City survives Herbert's current numbers make this the most counterintuitive offensive prediction: 937 passing yards, five touchdowns, seven interceptions and a 70.2 passer rating through five games. He has also absorbed 17 sacks. Against Denver, he managed 121 passing yards and was sacked five times. Receiving availability remains uncertain after Ladd McConkey dressed without playing, Quentin Johnston missed the game and Tre' Harris suffered a hamstring injury. Nevertheless, the prediction is that Herbert finally finds rhythm against a defense protecting a substantial lead. Two touchdown drives and a field goal produce 17 fourth-quarter points, forcing Kansas City to finish the game with its offense rather than coast. Walker provides that answer. The final forecast is Chiefs 38, Chargers 31: Kansas City remains unbeaten, but Los Angeles delivers a much stronger response than its record suggests. These are deliberately high-variance predictions, not the most likely outcomes. The underlying numbers favor Kansas City, but divisional familiarity and turnovers can make a comfortable matchup unpredictable. picks.blurb: Chiefs-Chargers Week 6 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Chiefs-Chargers Week 6 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jared Sapp Fri, October 16, 2026 at 6:00 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs host the Los Angeles Chargers , our writers predicted the final score and result. The Chargers may not have had the "Offseason Champions" accolades they frequently boast entering the season, but few expected an 0-5 start and making a case for the NFL's worst offense. They will try to get their first win on the road against a rested Chiefs squad coming off the bye. FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists Kansas City as 8.5-point home favorites. When last on the field, the Chiefs were tested but came out undefeated against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium in Week 4. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) The Chargers' 0-5 start is perhaps the season's biggest development. Still, a division game should always be taken seriously. Yes, it would be easier to name the Chargers not on this week's injury report than to speculate on who might play through a number of serious ailments. Yes, Mike McDaniel and Jim Harbaugh appear to be from different planets. But I'm going to plan a close game. Even if they play without longtime Travis Kelce nemesis Derwin James, I expect the Chargers defense to do what they've done for years: make this an ugly game that comes down to the fourth quarter. I expect Kansas City to come out on top, but I'm planning for a frustrating Sunday afternoon. Chiefs 24, Chargers 20 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) I did not expect this to be the season of the Chargers' undoing, but it has come at a good time for the Chiefs as they work their way back to the top of the AFC. The Chargers swept the Chiefs last season for the first time in nearly a decade, and Mahomes tore his ACL in the game that led to the Chiefs being eliminated from playoff contention. Despite the lopsided record and multiple players out, I still expect both teams to come out with plenty of juice. The Chargers to save their season, but the Chiefs will remind them that the AFC West still runs through Arrowhead Stadium despite the results of last season. Andy Reid off of a Bye Week is always an advantage, and his team will enter the game at nearly full health. With multiple starters out, I expect the Chargers to try to play the clock and play keep-away from Mahomes to help keep themselves in the game. The Chiefs offense will be without their key deep threat, Tyquan Thornton, but the combination of Mahomes and Kenneth Walker should be enough to get past the floundering Chargers. Chiefs 24, Chargers 14 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) I don't see the Chiefs having much trouble taking care of business against the Chargers on Sunday. We already know Andy Reid's track record coming off a bye week, and now he's facing an 0-5 Chargers team that's absolutely decimated by injuries. On top of that, Justin Herbert is playing some of the worst football of his career. I expect the Chiefs to come out sharp, handle business, and win this one comfortably. Chiefs 27, Chargers 13 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) The Chargers enter Week 6 at 0-5, making them one of the NFL's biggest surprises for all the wrong reasons. Justin Herbert and the offense have struggled under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, although the defense has kept them competitive. Injuries along the offensive line only make things tougher against an undefeated Chiefs team coming off a bye. On paper, Kansas City should win comfortably. But a winless division rival fighting for its season makes this a dangerous matchup. The Chargers would love nothing more than to hand the Chiefs their first loss. I don't see that happening Sunday. Despite injuries at wide receiver, Kansas City can continue leaning on Kenneth Walker III to keep the offense moving and create opportunities for Patrick Mahomes through play-action. Defensively, this feels like the week "Sack Nation" returns, with the Chiefs taking advantage of a depleted offensive line and making Herbert uncomfortable. Los Angeles will put up a fight, but Andy Reid's team will leave the bye ready to handle business. Chiefs 30, Chargers 20 Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) Your 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs are back to face another division opponent after the bye week. The winless Los Angeles Chargers come to town as the most disappointing team in the league after being a favorite breakout team for approximately 30 straight offseasons. They aren't untalented but have played poorly. That makes them dangerous at 0-5 with their backs aga the wall. Expect a close, bitter contest between division rivals, regardless of the records. Herbert will probably throw a couple of touchdowns, especially if his top 2WRs were back in the lineup. It's all going to come down to how well the Chiefs can execute. I expect the pass rush will get 3+ sacks. I expect Walker to have 100 total yards. I don't know what to expect from the Chiefs receivers. Will Cyrus Allen get a real shot? Will Xavier Worthy produce? Can they make up for injuries to Rice and Thornton? My prediction is that it won't be pretty, but it will be enough. Chiefs 27, Chargers 24 Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) Throw the records out for this one. To me, it doesn't matter the Chiefs are undefeated and the Chargers are winless. Every time these teams play, it seems to be a battle that comes down to the wire. And despite being winless and at times inept, the last three losses for the Chargers have all been by a score. These teams know each other, and I think it will be another close game. I don't expect a full game from Rashee Rice if he does play, and this leaves the receiver room as a major question mark. Expect a big game from Travis Kelce and for the pass rush to finally get home multiple times against the Chargers' beat up offensive line. Chiefs 30, Chargers 24 Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh is a franchise vampire. He drains the talent out of an organization and gets as many wins as he can before they shrivel up into a corpse. Unfortunately, the Chargers were already halfway to hospice by the time he took the reins. In the end, Ol' Khaki Bottle Glasses will pin the Chargers 30th-ranked offense on offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel (AKA The Vape Prince) to buy himself another year. But how is the Chargers 22nd ranked defense Captain E-Cig's fault? The Chiefs are coming out of the bye. Despite being banged up at wide receiver, as long as they don't play down to the competition, they should take care of business. Chiefs 36, Chargers 12 Nate Christensen Chiefs-Chargers has been exciting for the past couple of years and had a lot of intrigue coming into the season. That is no longer the case, as the Chargers are 0-5 and a complete train wreck. There's a good chance the Chargers' entire staff gets fired. They're incredibly banged up on offense, and the whole unit seems checked out. Division games can get weird, but with the Chiefs off a bye and the Chargers facing this opponent, I feel like they should easily cruise to a win. Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) When a team is in as much of a down spell as the Chargers are, the Chiefs have no excuse to let them up off the ground. Los Angeles' incredible injury report, which named more than 20 players on Thursday, reflects how broken the team has looked over five games. Quarterback Justin Herbert hasn't elevated the team with his own play, so it's on Kansas City to do what it takes to ensure he doesn't get a bounce-back performance. That's what it will take to beat the Chiefs in Arrowhead on Sunday. Off a bye week, the team should relish this opportunity at home and take care of business. Expect defensive tackle Chris Jones to come off a bye week and lead a resurgent pass rush, taking advantage of strong man coverage on the back end to tally multiple sacks on Herbert in an imperfect victory that moves the team to 5-0. Chiefs 23, Chargers 17 2026 Standings Maurice Elston Dakota Watson Nate Chrstensen The AP panel was split in Week 4 between predicting a comfortable or a close victory for Kansas City . All nine staffers on the panel did correctly predict the Chiefs would win. Jared Sapp (34-31) and Ron Kopp Jr. (23-20) did predict three-point margins. Jared tied with Matt Stagner's 31-24 prediction to lead the way with only eight points of error. Matt has been the panel's overall most accurate member through the season's quarter mark. 92.4% of our readers predicted a Chiefs victory , with 60 .3% anticipating a close score. *To calculate a prediction's points of error, the differences between the prediction and the actual score in point spread, home team score, and away team score are added together. For example, a prediction calls for a 17-10 Chiefs win. They end up winning 16-10, so there were two points of error: the point spread was off by one point, the Kansas City score missed by one point, and the opponent's score was predicted correctly. But if the Chiefs lose the game 17-10, there were 28 points of error in the prediction: the point spread was off by 14 (the difference between +7 and -7), and both scores were off by 7.
