Mandatory Credit: Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Joshua Schulman Fri, October 16, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs should be well-rested coming off their bye , but Andy Reid's squad is getting right back into the action with a divisional matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers. It's a classic example of an unstoppable force versus an immovable object: an unbeaten Chiefs team hosting a winless Los Angeles squad desperate for answers. KC is among the favorites in the AFC to reach the Super Bowl in early projections. Patrick Mahomes is back to his MVP form after tearing his ACL against this same Chargers team a year ago, and the addition of running back Kenneth Walker has transformed the offense into a juggernaut. Can LA turn its campaign around and pull off an upset in Arrowhead Stadium this weekend? Let's take a look at what ESPN's Matchup Predictor says heading into kickoff. Chargers at Chiefs: ESPN Matchup Predictor Gives Prediction Justin Herbert and Mahomes have had some great battles over the years, though this matchup comes under unusual circumstances. The Chargers haven't started a season 0-5 since the team was still based in San Diego more than 20 years ago. Dec 14, 2025; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) looks to pass against the Los Angeles Chargers during the second quarter at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect ESPN Matchup Predictor Chances at Victory: Chiefs 73.5%, Chargers 26.3%. Despite their dismal record, the Chargers still have a decent chance of coming out on top Sunday, according to the matchup predictor. For context, before the bye, the computer model only gave the Chiefs a 3.5% greater chance of beating an undefeated Raiders team on the road. Chiefs on SI's Take The Chargers are far out of the divisional race and likely out of playoff contention, but Jim Harbaugh's squad isn't as awful as its start suggests. It's hard to imagine a team of this caliber finishing with just four or five wins. LA suffered inexplicable defeats to the Raiders and Cardinals early in the season. Just when they appeared poised to finally get into the win column last week, the Chargers collapsed in the fourth quarter against fellow AFC West opponent, the Denver Broncos. The matchup predictor gives the Chargers better than a one-in-four chance against KC, suggesting a win may not be too far off the radar for Los Angeles, whether it comes this week or next. The Chargers can't head into November without a single victory... right? Oct 11, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) greets Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) after the game at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect One thing to monitor is the Chiefs' receiving situation, as Tyquan Thornton will be sidelined for an extended period and Rashee Rice is likely to miss the game with a lingering hamstring injury. That means the offense will lean heavily on Walker and Travis Kelce to carry the load. If the Chargers are going to put up a fight, Herbert has to pick up his play - point-blank, period. It's been a humiliating stretch for someone who is usually considered one of the AFC's best signal-callers, as he's thrown seven interceptions to his five touchdowns in 2026. picks.headline: Chiefs vs. Chargers Preview: Kansas City Looks to Stay Undefeated Against Los Angeles
picks.blurb: Chiefs vs. Chargers Preview: Kansas City Looks to Stay Undefeated Against Los Angeles - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Photo by: David Brytus Stephan Stroud Thu, October 15, 2026 at 8:27 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs return from their bye week looking to keep their perfect start alive when they host the Los Angeles Chargers in an important AFC West matchup on Sunday, October 18. Kansas City enters the game at 4-0 after winning its first four contests, while Los Angeles is searching for its first victory after opening the season 0-5. The Chargers will have a difficult challenge at Arrowhead Stadium as they try to turn their season around against one of the AFC's early standouts. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. Eastern on CBS. Patrick Mahomes Leads the Chiefs Quarterback Patrick Mahomes has helped Kansas City get off to an impressive start in 2026. Through four games, Mahomes has thrown for 1,037 yards and nine touchdowns with just two interceptions, giving the Chiefs a productive passing attack. Kansas City has also found success on the ground with running back Kenneth Walker III. Walker has rushed for 537 yards and four touchdowns, averaging 6.2 yards per carry. His ability to produce explosive runs has given opposing defenses another major concern beyond Mahomes. Head coach Andy Reid will look to keep that offensive balance going against a Chargers defense that has shown the ability to pressure quarterbacks. The Chiefs will also monitor wide receiver Rashee Rice, who missed practice Wednesday with a hamstring injury. Justin Herbert Faces a Difficult Challenge For Los Angeles, quarterback Justin Herbert needs to help an offense that has struggled to produce consistently. Herbert has thrown for 937 yards, five touchdowns and seven interceptions through five games. The Chargers have averaged only 16.8 points per game, making offensive improvement a major priority. Herbert has the arm talent to challenge Kansas City's secondary, but he will need better protection and consistent production from his receiving corps. Injuries have complicated that task, with several Los Angeles wide receivers and defensive starters appearing on the team's injury report this week. Head coach Jim Harbaugh must find a way to help his team limit mistakes and sustain drives. A stronger running game could ease the pressure on Herbert and help keep Mahomes off the field. Andy Reid vs. Jim Harbaugh The coaching matchup adds another layer to this divisional rivalry. Reid has Kansas City playing efficient football on both sides of the ball, while Harbaugh is trying to find answers after a difficult opening month. The Chargers swept the Chiefs in 2025, adding extra motivation for Kansas City to protect its home field and maintain control of the AFC West rivalry. A Critical AFC West Matchup Kansas City has an opportunity to improve to 5-0 and continue building momentum after its bye week. Los Angeles, meanwhile, needs a complete performance to avoid falling further behind in the division. Mahomes and Walker give the Chiefs multiple ways to attack, while Herbert will need to deliver a more consistent performance to help the Chargers compete. With the Chiefs chasing another strong start and the Chargers desperate to get their season moving, Sunday's matchup carries plenty of importance for both teams.

picks.headline: Chargers-Chiefs Game Preview: 5 Questions with Arrowhead Pride
picks.blurb: Chargers-Chiefs Game Preview: 5 Questions with Arrowhead Pride - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Chargers-Chiefs Game Preview: 5 Questions with Arrowhead Pride LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 04: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs reacts prior to the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Steve Marcus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Michael Peterson Fri, October 16, 2026 at 4:57 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This week we were joined by Maurice Elston of our Chiefs sister community, Arrowhead Pride, to help us preview this week's matchup with Kansas City. With these two teams on two completely different trajectories this season, this game may not be appointment watching for most, but anyone who follows the AFC West knows it's still likely to be a surprisingly competitive game between divisional rivals. Let's go ahead and dive right in! 1.) The Chiefs are back. I don't think anyone can say otherwise. Can you give us a TL/DR explanation on what happened last season and what the Chiefs did to quickly get back into the NFL's elite? Last year, the Chiefs lacked discipline across the board. There were costly penalties, turnovers and dropped passes at unfortunate times, and those mistakes completely changed their fortunes in close games. Kansas City went 12-0 in one-score games in 2024, including the playoffs, before going 1-9 in those situations last season. That was probably the biggest difference between the two years. You pair that with Xavier Worthy's shoulder injury, Rashee Rice's six-game suspension and several injuries along the offensive line, and it became one of those seasons where everything seemed to go wrong. I also think all those extended playoff runs and trips to the Super Bowl finally caught up with them. The Chiefs turned it around quickly because they identified their problems and made the necessary changes. They reshuffled the coaching staff, bringing back Eric Bieniemy as offensive coordinator and hiring a demanding wide receivers coach in Chad O'Shea. Those moves restored some of the discipline, energy and accountability that were missing. They also understood that their style of play needed to change. Defenses had adjusted to Kansas City by taking away the big plays, generating pressure with four rushers and dropping seven into coverage. The addition of Kenneth Walker III and a renewed commitment to the running game have given the offense a different identity. With the dominant interior offensive linemen the Chiefs already had, that change has helped them return to the NFL's elite quickly. 2.) Signing Kenneth Walker may end up being the most-impactful free agent signed this offseason. How was that signing first received by the Chiefs fan base and how much has he met or surpassed expectations? The signing was received extremely well by Chiefs fans. Walker was the running back many fans wanted, but I don't think most people believed Brett Veach would spend the money necessary to get him. His three-year deal initially looked like a significant investment at a position where the Chiefs traditionally haven't spent much money. However, after Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson helped reset the running back market, Walker's contract began looking like an excellent value. I think he has already surpassed expectations. You knew the Chiefs were getting a great player and a reigning Super Bowl MVP, but 537 rushing yards and 621 yards from scrimmage through four games is beyond what anyone reasonably could have expected. He has completely changed the identity of the offense, given the Chiefs a home-run threat in the backfield and made defenses respect the run on every play. 3.) If you were Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, how would you go about attacking this Chiefs defense? Which players/matchups would you attempt to exploit? If I'm Mike McDaniel, I'm attacking the Chiefs similarly to how the Raiders did. The best opportunity is in the middle of the field, where you can force Kansas City's linebackers and safeties to defend in space. I would use running backs and tight ends on quick passes, option routes and crossing concepts designed to create favorable matchups against the linebackers. I would also test L'Jarius Sneed in the slot. Teams have had some success targeting him with quick passes this season, particularly when they can prevent Kansas City's pass rush from getting home. If the Chargers can get the ball out quickly, attack Sneed in the slot and force the Chiefs' linebackers and safeties into difficult coverage assignments, they should be able to move the football. 4.) If you were Chargers defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary, how are you attempting to put a lid on this Chiefs offense? How should teams prepare for Kansas City when they now have such a strong rushing attack to go with Patrick Mahomes? This is where it becomes much more difficult. Defenses can no longer sit back with light boxes, put extra defenders into coverage and dare the Chiefs to run. Kansas City has proven it will remain committed to the running game, and Kenneth Walker has shown he can handle a heavy workload while also breaking explosive plays. If I'm Chris O'Leary, I'm devoting extra resources to stopping Walker and challenging Kansas City's wide receivers with man-to-man coverage. The Chiefs' receivers haven't consistently beaten man coverage this season, and the group is now depleted. Tyquan Thornton is sidelined with an ankle injury, while Rashee Rice is dealing with a hamstring injury and might not be 100% even if he plays. I would make the Chiefs' available wide receivers prove they can consistently separate against man coverage. That comes with the obvious risk of leaving your defensive backs exposed against Patrick Mahomes, but allowing Walker to control the game would make Kansas City almost impossible to stop. 5.) Let's go ahead and top this off with a final score prediction and few lines on how you see this game shaking out. Are the Chiefs going to win in a blowout? Will it be close? The Chargers should enter this game in desperation mode. They are 0-5 and badly need a victory, while the Chiefs are 4-0, coming off their bye week and probably feeling very confident. That creates the ingredients for a potential trap game. On paper, Kansas City is clearly the better team, especially considering the number of injuries the Chargers are dealing with. However, this is still an AFC West rivalry, and these games are normally competitive regardless of the teams' records. I expect the Chargers to keep it close through the first three quarters before the Chiefs begin to separate late. Kansas City's running game and fresh defensive front should eventually wear Los Angeles down. Chiefs 30, Chargers 20.

home.blurb: NFL insider weighs in on when Tyreek Hill could be eyeing a return in the Kansas City Chiefs The Athletic's NFL insider Michael Silver added, "In the wake of those injuries, the Chiefs have already reached out to Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, to express their interest…” After undergoing surgeries and being released by the Miami Dolphins, the star player has been continuing his rehabilitation with a target return window around November 2026. Tyreek Hill, the former Miami Dolphins’ wide receiver, has been a topic of discussion for the last few weeks while his personal life and broken marriage with Keeta Vaccaro has dominated headlines. While now he has been ordered to pay $500,000 to his estranged wife, an NFL insider is hinted that when things between Tyreek Hill and his former team, the Kansas City Chiefs, can finally progress. The Athletic's NFL insider Michael Silver continued, "They'd have to be satisfied with the receiver's recovery, but there would likely be no other obstacles on the organization's end. However, neither the 8 time Pro Bowler Tyreek Hill nor his former team, the Kansas City Chiefs, have confirmed the speculations yet. I did say last week I thought a deal could happen at any time…” Tyreek Hill’s agent Drew Rosenhaus continued, "But in the NFL, it really is day to day. home.headline: Chiefs’ WR injury woes could be fixed with one major trade
home.blurb: Knox recently named the Chiefs as a possible landing spot for disgruntled Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy, suggesting the Chiefs could send the Browns a conditional 2027 fifth-round pick in return. “According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, it’s ‘pretty well known around the league’ that Jeudy is available,” Knox wrote . “Per Schultz, the Browns would prefer to get a third- or fourth-round pick in exchange for the receiver, though that may be difficult. “The 27-year-old struggled through last season and has fallen out of the game plan this year as Concepcion, Boston, and tight end Harold Fannin Jr. have become the go-to targets. Still, Jeudy is a talented pass-catcher who made the Pro Bowl just two years ago following a 1,229-yard season. His skill set hasn’t disappeared, and his 2026 base salary of $1.5 million should appeal to budget-conscious teams.” The Kansas City Chiefs have been pretty snake-bitten when it comes to keeping healthy wide receivers on their roster. Second-leading receiver Tyquan Thornton suffered a gruesome ankle injury nearly two weeks ago against the Las Vegas Raiders that will likely sideline him the rest of the season. Rashee Rice could miss some time with hamstring and knee injuries, and both Jeff Caldwell and Jimmy Holiday have been on injured reserve since the end of August. As things sit now, Xavier Worthy (14 catches, 133 yards, one touchdown), Jalen Royals (three catches, 17 yards, one TD), Cyrus Allen and Nikko Remigio are the only healthy WRs on Kansas City’s roster — and the latter two haven’t recorded a catch this season, which is why Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report thinks they should look to upgrade the position. Jeudy (eight catches for 81 yards in five games) has been almost a non-factor this season with the emergence of Boston and Concepcion. However, he had a 90-reception, 1,229-yard, four-TD season just two years ago. In Kansas City he would see much more than the three targets per game he’s currently getting in Cleveland. Jeudy would also give quarterback Patrick Mahomes the kind of reliable big-play target he’s been missing ever since the team traded away Tyreek Hill. NFL insider Adam Schefter revealed the latest injury update for Rice in a post to his official Twitter account on October 14, just days before Kansas City is set to face the Chargers in a rivalry matchup at Arrowhead Stadium: While Rice could hypothetically take the field to face the Chargers this weekend despite his injury, Kansas City's coaching staff is likely to be cautious with their injured wideout, especially after speedy receiver Tyquan Thornton suffered a serious lower-body injury in Week 4 that may prove to be a season-ender. They looked like two very different teams in those losses, the first being a competitive. hard-fought loss to the Chiefs at home, and the second a blowout loss to the Patriots in New England. This game brings the Raiders back to Vegas, but has them facing off against the top offense in the NFL. Can they rally from their recent loss and bounce back? Or will their losing streak reach three games? I gathered the Raiders Wire staff to get their picks for the Raiders game against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. Here are those picks. Justin Melo -- Bills 30, Raiders 17 The Las Vegas Raiders defense will struggle to stop Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills' high-octane offense. The Raiders aren't ready to compete at this level yet. Marvin Uzor -- Bills 31, Raiders 24 Yes we can all agree that the Raiders have enough firepower with Kirk Cousins and Brock Bowers to keep this close. But giving up 102 points in three games, honestly doesn't inspire much confidence against Josh Allen and James Cook. So I really think Buffalo pulls away late. Lamarr Fields -- Bills 35, Raiders 31 The Raiders offense will put up points and compete, but Josh Allen and James Cook will be too much for the Raiders' defense. I think the Raiders will run the ball well and Brock Bowers will have a huge game, but Allen's dual-threat capability will hurt the Raiders. Lance Fernandez -- Bills 35, Raiders 24 The energy for the Raiders will be there, considering that they will be playing at home. However, they are 29th in rushing yards allowed per game, and that's a troubling fact when the Raiders are set to face Josh Allen and James Cook. If Buffalo's run game stalls, Allen can air it out and the Raiders' secondary isn't a sure bet in stopping the Bills' passing attack. The Raiders will get their points, especially with Brock Bowers back in the lineup. But an unhealthy Ashton Jeanty and a questionable offensive line means the Raiders might not have enough to match the Bills toe-to-toe. Levi Damien -- Bills 31, Raiders 26 No matter how surprising the Raiders had been in their first four weeks, nothing the Bills are doing is a surprise. They have elite players on offense who can have been putting up big numbers against some very good teams this season. The Patriots had their way with the Raiders defense last week, posting 45 points on them with relative ease. Though this week the Raiders should have a bit more success on offense, they can't keep pace with the Bills. Pick totals: Bills 5, Raiders 0 Average score: Bills 32, Raiders 24 It's unanimous. Everyone sees the Bills coming into Allegiant and leaving with a win. All have the Bills scoring at least 30 points. There is a bit more range in terms of how much the Raiders are expected to score. The Houston Texans just got their first win. The Dallas Cowboys can't get out of their own way, and the Buffalo Bills are mauling everyone in their way. It's been a wacky start to the season, which has made our NFL picks and predictions for every game each week a bit more difficult than I expected. We're having to adjust our perceptions and expectations on the fly, and we're still in the mix as we head into what should be a fascinating Week 6. Zach Rotman came out of the bullpen for me last week and came through with a solid week. Many, many thanks to him for helping the cause, but I'm back in the saddle now. Let's hope I don't make this thing go any further off the rails, but let's dive right into this fun slate with our NFL picks for Week 6 as we make predictions both straight-up and against the spread for all 14 games on the slate this week. Toughest NFL Week 6 prediction to make Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Buffalo Bills at Las Vegas Raiders (+5.5) The Buffalo Bills have been rolling, including toppling the Rams in overtime in Los Angeles on Monday night. Stop me if you've heard this one before, but Buffalo has one of the NFL's best offenses behind Josh Allen and it doesn't seem like there's a defense in the league that's going to be able to stop this team from scoring 30 points - they're quite literally averaging 32.7 points per game after the first five games of the year. Meanwhile, the Raiders have certainly fallen back to earth a bit, losing two straight after their 3-0 start to the season. At the same time, the Bills defense is the same problem it's been for the past few years. It seems like Buffalo has to produce at this level offensively to win games because the defense is going to give it up. While the Raiders might not be a surprise contender, they still look like a quite competent football team behind Kirk Cousins and, while Buffalo will be able to score on their defense, they're still averaging 26.4 points per game on the year. I think Buffalo still has the offensive firepower against a middling defense to get the win in this game. But with it being in Vegas against a team that has a legitimate pulse, it's going to be another shootout and one that could likely be decided by a field goal once again. 5.5 points is a bit too many, so we'll take the Raiders against the spread and pray. Easiest NFL Week 6 pick on the board Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Los Angeles Chargers at Kansas City Chiefs (-8.5) This line could've been two touchdowns and I'm still taking the Kansas City Chiefs over the division rival Chargers. For starters, what has LA shown this season to make you believe they have a chance in Arrowhead in Week 6? No, seriously. There's been little evidence to think that this game will be close as the Chiefs have been absolutely rolling on both sides of the ball while Justin Herbert delivers the worst season of his career, the Chargers defense is middling at its best and the self-inflicted wounds in each game from LA multiply likes the heads of a hydra. If that weren't enough, Andy Reid is famously one of the most lethal head coaches when his team is coming off of the bye week. This isn't to say that the Chiefs are a perfect team as I maintain that they still need to find some more upgrades at wide receiver, especially after the gnarly Tyquan Thornton injury. While that may be true, though, they are a far better coached and more talented team than the winless Chargers and I wouldn't be surprised if this game was lopsided and out of hand early in favor of the home side. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dallas Cowboys (+1.5) at Green Bay Packers Coming off of a home loss to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels and the previously winless Buccaneers, naturally I'm taking the Dallas Cowboys to go on the road to Lambeau and beat the Packers as underdogs. What about this doesn't make sense to you? Yes, the optics look strange. However, this isn't about expecting the Cowboys hiring Mike Pettine to essentially help out new defensive coordinator Christian Parker drastically improving the defense, though it can't hurt. It's more about this being a likely shootout between these two teams because, despite what happened to Tyson Bagent and the Bears, I still don't trust Green Bay on that side of the ball. Furthermore, I also still don't trust the Packers run game, even against Dallas. Expect this game to go back and forth throughout the action, but I believe the Cowboys are going to have more offensive firepower and some adjustments on the side of the ball you can actually trust Dallas on to attack Green Bay throughout. They might not come up with many stops of their own, but they'll have enough to pull out the win. Plus, just from a narrative perspective, if ever there was a time for the Cowboys to keep their fans from abandoning ship, it's a game like this, and this franchise has been masterful at doing exactly that over the years. picks.blurb: Bills vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 6 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Bills vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 6 Tim Crean, ClutchPoints Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:44 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Buffalo Bills face off against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6. This matchup between the 4-1 Bills and the 3-2 Raiders gets a prime spot in the late Sunday window as one of the best games of the week. These two original AFC franchises haven't played a game with meaningful stakes for both teams since the 1993 "Just Freeze Baby" Divisional Round game . Now, as both sides come into this game with winning records, let's make some bold Bills-Raiders predictions. Start your Raiders in fantasy football The Bills are their own worst enemy so far this season, as they love to gift their opponents chances to stay in the game. Whether it is shockingly cavalier Josh Allen interceptions, infuriating James Cook fumbles, or the fact that the defense (outside of Deone Walker and Gregory Rousseau) looks like it has no clue what it is doing right now, Buffalo loves keeping the other team in the game. Sunday will be no different, as fans should expect at least two turnovers from the Bills' offense and long stretches where the Raiders' O looks like the 2007 New England Patriots. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) That means big games from the Raiders' defense, Kirk Cousins, Brock Bowers, Ashton Jeanty, and maybe even the likes of Mike Washington Jr., Michael Mayer, and Tre Tucker. So, for all you fantasy football players out there, any Raiders on your roster should be a good play in Week 6 . Josh Allen delivers again Despite the mediocre (or worse) play at times from the Bills' offensive line, wide receivers, tight end, and running backs, and defensive back seven, the Bills are 4-1 and leading the AFC East thanks to one man: Brandon Beane. Just kidding! He's the reason the rest of the team is struggling so much. The real reason is Josh Allen. Through five weeks, Allen is still the betting favorite for NFL MVP this year. Yes, Brock Bowers is playing great, and Patrick Mahomes is back, but if you define MVP as the players whose absence would tank his team's chances the most, Allen has to be the answer. Monday night's dramatic OT win over the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams came courtesy of 210 yards passing and a staggering 121 yards rushing from the Bills QB. Sure, he threw his obligatory head-scratching pick in the first half, but in the second, it was a one-man battle with 53 Rams players, and the singular man won. Against the Raiders, expect more of the same. Vegas has an improved defense this season and an incredible pass rusher in Maxx Crosby, but that only means Allen will be forced to take off even more as usual. And with his receivers getting minimal separation and Cook's suspect ball security, it will be all Allen, all the time in Week 6. Bills 31, Raiders 24 This won't be a cakewalk for the Bills by any means, as the Raiders are one of (if not) the most improved teams in the league. We know Cousins is a professional QB, the Raiders have some incredible young offensive weapons, and Klint Kubiak seems like a legit NFL head coach with an incredibly bright future. Allen doesn't have those last two things, as his skill position core is the exact same as last year, as long as D.J. Moore is out injured and his "new" head coach is just the same offensive coordinator who couldn't get it done the past three seasons, but with a more impressive title. Nevertheless, Allen should be able to will his Bills to victory over the Raiders in Week 6 just by sheer force of talent and will. As good as Las Vegas has looked at times this season, they are probably a year or two away from being legit contenders. That's why we'll take the Buffalo to win here, and to do so by slightly more than the -5.5-point spread suggests. picks.blurb: Bills vs. Raiders Preview: Buffalo Looks to Keep Rolling Against Las Vegas - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Bills vs. Raiders Preview: Buffalo Looks to Keep Rolling Against Las Vegas Photo by: Bob DeChiara Stephan Stroud Thu, October 15, 2026 at 8:31 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Buffalo Bills head to Las Vegas on Sunday for a Week 6 matchup against the Raiders, with both teams looking to strengthen their positions in the AFC playoff race. Buffalo enters the game at 4-1 after an exciting 37-34 overtime victory over the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night. The Raiders, meanwhile, are 3-2 after suffering a 45-17 loss to the New England Patriots. With the Bills carrying one of the league's most productive offenses and Las Vegas looking to bounce back, Sunday's matchup at Allegiant Stadium presents an important test for both teams. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. Eastern on CBS. Josh Allen Leads Buffalo's Explosive Offense Quarterback Josh Allen remains the centerpiece of Buffalo's offense. Through five games, Allen has thrown for 1,249 yards and seven touchdowns while adding eight rushing touchdowns. His ability to create plays with both his arm and legs makes him one of the most difficult quarterbacks to defend. Allen was particularly dangerous against the Rams, throwing for 342 yards and two touchdowns while rushing for 121 yards. His performance helped Buffalo survive a back-and-forth contest and improve to 4-1. Running back James Cook has also been productive, rushing for 532 yards through five games. His speed and ability to create explosive plays give the Bills another weapon that Las Vegas must account for. Head coach Joe Brady will look to keep the offense balanced while helping Allen avoid costly turnovers. Buffalo has committed nine giveaways over its last three games, making ball security an important focus heading into Sunday. Raiders Need a Strong Response Las Vegas will look to quarterback Kirk Cousins to help the offense recover from its disappointing performance against New England. Cousins has thrown for 1,269 yards and 12 touchdowns through five games, giving the Raiders a capable passing attack. Tight end Brock Bowers has been one of Cousins' primary targets, recording 312 receiving yards and three touchdowns. His ability to create mismatches could be especially important against a Buffalo defense that has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks. The Raiders will also rely on running back Ashton Jeanty , who has rushed for 291 yards this season. Establishing the ground game could help Las Vegas control possession and prevent Allen from spending too much time on the field. Head coach Klint Kubiak will need his team to improve its offensive line play and limit mistakes after the loss to New England. Former Las Vegas Raiders first-round pick and current Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs received some welcoming news on October 16th. The NFL is removing him from the Commissioner Exempt List on October 19th, which means he'll be eligible to play in the Packers' Week 7 game on October 25th after missing six games. "The NFL initiated an investigation under the Personal Conduct Policy following Jacobs' arrest in May," the NFL wrote in a statement. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. That's something that seems hard to bounce back from, because everyone looks dumb. Stroud, Green Bay gets its ground game rolling against Dallas, and Justin Herbert breaks out of an ugly slump Getty Images Anything can happen in the NFL , and the start to Week 6 of the 2026 season certainly hammered home that fact. In the Denver Broncos (4-2) 17-14 "Thursday Night Football" overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks , they triumphed at home despite averaging 2.9 yards per play. That's the fewest in Sean Payton's 318-game head-coaching career, and Denver's 168 total yards of offense ranked as their fewest in a victory since Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback John Elway's first start as a rookie in 1983. Quarterback Bo Nix , who ranks dead last in the NFL in yards per pass attempt at 5.6, improved to a 13-3 career record in games when he averages six yards per pass attempt or fewer, the best of all-time minimum 15 starts per CBS Sports Research, after averaging 4.0 yards per pass attempt on Thursday. All other active quarterbacks have a combined .283 winning percentage in starts where they average six yards per pass attempt or fewer. That's absolutely unfathomable. What other hijinks could take place across the rest of the NFL's Week 6 slate? Here is a look at five bold predictions. Packers run for over 100 yards for first time in 2026 vs. Cowboys The Green Bay Packers are back above .500 after quarterback Jordan Love's laser show (367 yards and 2 passing touchdowns while completing 25 of his 31 throws) in a 31-7 beatdown of the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field in Week 5. Now that they have a winning record, they're now the owners of the third-fewest rushing yards per game (60.4) by any team above .500 through five games of a season in league history, per CBS Sports Research. Green Bay's NFL-worst rushing offense also ranks as the fewest rushing yards per game through games of any season in the Packers' 106-season franchise history. Some of that has to do with the absence of running back Josh Jacobs , who is on the commissioner's exempt list after being charged with two misdemeanors, and some of that has to do with the team's beat-up offensive line. However, the offensive line has stabilized with veterans Laken Tomlinson and Travis Glover stabilizing the team's guard play. That's one of the reasons why the Packers will run for over 100 yards as a team for the first time in 2026 against the Dallas Cowboys on "Sunday Night Football." The others are that Green Bay running back MarShawn Lloyd is a freight train at 5 feet 9 inches tall and 220 pounds, and the Cowboys have the league's worst run defense (168.4 rushing yards allowed per game). Dallas allowed the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to go off for 241 yards rushing, their most in a game since 2024, on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 5. Facing a leaky defense like that and Lloyd fresh off running through Bears cornerback Jaylon Johnson's face for a touchdown in Week 5, Lloyd and the Packers cross the century mark on the ground for the first time this season. Marshawn Lloyd trucks a guy on his way to the end zone 😤 @CHIvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NNcSwQfTOU Marvin Harrison Jr. has first 100-yard receiving game since his rookie year Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud is quietly playing efficient football: he has the fifth-most passing attempts without an interception (185) through five games in NFL history while throwing for the fourth-most passing yards in the NFL (1,402) this season. The Texans (1-4) have a high-volume passing offense this season because of their struggling rushing offense, and that will lead to Houston's newest player, 2024 fourth overall pick wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. , thriving in his team debut against the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1). How much will he soar in his first game back with his former Ohio State Buckeyes teammate in Stroud? Harrison Jr. will produce his first 100-yard receiving game since his rookie year in 2024 and just the third overall 100-yard receiving game of his young career on Sunday. He and Stroud were Ohio State teammates for two seasons from 2021 to 2022, and Harrison Jr.'s 14 receiving touchdowns when Stroud was the starting quarterback in 2022 are tied for the third most in a single season in Buckeyes' history. Harrison Jr. also set or tied career-highs in catches (77), receiving yards (1,263) and receiving touchdowns (14) in that 2022 season with Stroud. Houston will be celebrating their newest trade acquisition's 100-yard game when the clock hits zero at Wembley Stadium on Sunday. Justin Herbert ends fourth-quarter turnover streak and multi-passing touchdown drought vs. Chiefs The Los Angeles Chargers are injury-plagued and riding the struggle bus at 0-5 to start 2026. Pro Bowl quarterback Justin Herbert is tied for the most interceptions (seven) and turnovers (nine) in the NFL this season, and he has a couple of ugly streaks going against him. He has five consecutive games with a fourth-quarter turnover, making him the first quarterback since Charlie Frye in 2006 to do that. Herbert also hasn't thrown for multiple passing touchdowns in a game in his last seven games, the longest such streak of his career. However, he will play a clean fourth quarter and throw multiple touchdown passes against the 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead on Sunday. The last time the Chiefs were on the field in Week 4, 38-year-old Kirk Cousins threw for 365 yards, 2 touchdowns and an interception on 31 of 52 passes in a narrow 30-27 Chiefs win. Herbert will snap out of his funk and raise his level to go toe-to-toe with Mahomes by having a clean fourth quarter and throwing multiple touchdowns for the first time in a while. Jets' Geno Smith throws first interception of 2026 at Patriots Geno Smith is on an incredible public relations campaign in 2026 with the New York Jets . After leading the NFL with 17 interceptions as a Las Vegas Raider in 2025, he hasn't thrown any through five games this season. Smith has six passing touchdowns to no interceptions this season, a stark contrast from his touchdown-to-interception ratio at this time a year ago when he had the same number of touchdown passes (six) but with nine interceptions. He is only the second quarterback in NFL history with no interceptions through five starts, after leading the league in interceptions the previous season, and is tied with Vinny Testaverde, also with the Jets, back in 2001, per CBS Sports Research. However, Smith will throw his first interception of the season in Week 6 at the New England Patriots . Patriots All-Pro cornerback Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) is on track to return this week, fully practicing on Thursday after being limited on Wednesday. In his first game back after a two-game absence, Gonzalez will intercept Smith for the veteran's first interception of 2026. Saints won't cover as road favorite at Giants Yes, your eyes don't deceive you. According to DraftKings Sportsbook , the 1-4 New Orleans Saints are favored by 1.5 points over the 3-1-1 New York Giants on the road at MetLife Stadium. Perhaps the ugliness of the NFC East leader's 27-27 tie at the Washington Commanders in Week 5 is pushing the spread in favor of the Saints. Maybe it's the allure of New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough , whose 1,299 passing yards rank as the seventh-most in the NFL. Regardless, that positions the Saints to win on Sunday, as they have covered in seven consecutive road games, the longest active road cover streak in the entire NFL, per CBS Sports Research. However, the Saints' road cover streak will be broken on Sunday because Jameis Winston plays a more efficient brand of football than Shough. Sure, Winston's 57.6% is the second-worst in the NFL among 31 qualified quarterbacks in 2026, but he is starting to turn a corner and find a groove as an NFL starting quarterback once again. He is the first Giants quarterback with three-plus passing touchdowns in consecutive games since Eli Manning in 2016, and Winston didn't throw a single interception after having two in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals a couple of weeks ago. On the other hand, Shough has a turnover problem: his eight this season are the third-most in the league. The Cowboys fell victim to the trap game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Dallas was heavily favored, and rightly so, as Tampa Bay was 0-4 and starting an undrafted rookie quarterback. But Dallas failed to so much as show up and fell to 2-3 on the year. The Packers, on the other hand, absolutely throttled the Chicago Bears in what was far and away Green Bay's best game on both sides of the ball. Now, all of the talk of the Packers' demise has been shelved. These two teams squared off last season and battled to a 40-40 tie. Before that, Green Bay had beaten Dallas in eight of their last nine meetings. Will the Packers continue their dominance over the Cowboys? Or will Dallas flip the script and pull out a win? The Packers had struggled offensively over the first four contests, but they found their rhythm in Week 5 by torching the Bears with the deep ball. Defending the pass has been a major issue for the Cowboys this season, with Dallas ranking 21st. That doesn't even do justice for how bad it has really been. The Cowboys' ranking would be even worse if teams weren't abusing Christian Parker's unit on the ground. The good news for the Cowboys is the Packers haven't been able to run the football with any semblance of success, although Dallas presents a perfect get-right opportunity with their league-worst showing against the run this season. Green Bay has also struggled to stop the run, ranking 24th, but the Cowboys aren't running the ball like they did last season and it remains to be seen if they can capitalize on Green Bay's woes. Another problem for the Cowboys is the Packers are giving up the fifth-fewest yards per game through the air and if that holds true this week and the run game doesn't get on track, it's going to be tough sledding for Dallas' offense. Joey Porter Jr.'s return is going to make a dent in Dallas' passing game struggles, but the Cowboys still have the other side of the field to defend and DaRon Bland has proven incapable of doing that. The slot is a another concern if Caleb Downs is still playing most or all of his snaps at safety like he has amid the Cowboys' slew of injuries at safety. The Cowboys will get their points to keep this game close, but we're highly skeptical Dallas' secondary and pass-rush will do enough to keep Green Bay's passing attack at bay enough to emerge victorious. away.headline: Breaking down Packers' final injury report of Week 6 vs. Cowboys
away.blurb: LG Aaron Banks (toe/knee): He practiced in a limited capacity all week, but it's his first week back from a multi-week injury. More than likely, the Packers will go with Laken Tomlinson at left guard against the Cowboys. Eventually, the Packers will have to make a long-term decision on their preferred starter at the position. DL Anthony Campbell (ankle) : His likely return from an ankle injury is coming at a good time considering the injury situation along the defensive front. It's possible Campbell will need to play double-digit snaps behind Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks and Chris McClellan on Sunday night. CB Brandon Cisse (hip): An unexpected addition to the injury report. Cisse injured his hip and was limited on Friday, creating the dreaded late-week injury and potential need to scramble for answers at a key position. Carrington Valentine would likely start if Cisse can't go. Depth at cornerback is under real stress ahead of matchup with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. WR Savion Williams (ankle): Is the second-year receiver ready to return from an ankle injury that had him on injured reserve to start the season? A natural replacement option for Skyy Moore, who is out, Williams could provide help as a gadget weapon on offense and in the return game if the Packers activate him to the 53-man roster before Sunday night. WR/KR Skyy Moore (ankle): The Packers' primary kick and punt returner injured his ankle last week and wasn't able to practice this week. It's possible the Packers will activate Savion Williams to help make up for Moore's absence in the return game and at receiver. away.headline: Eagles poach QB from Cowboys amid Jalen Hurts blood clot uncertainty
away.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles plan to poach a quarterback from an NFC East rival in the wake of Jalen Hurts' unexpected injury . The Eagles are signing Joe Milton III off the practice squad of the Dallas Cowboys , according to multiple reports on Friday, Oct. 16. This was the start of Milton's second season with the Cowboys after being traded to Dallas by the New England Patriots in exchange for a fifth-round pick in April 2025 . NFL rules stipulate that a player signed off another team's practice squad must be placed on the 53-man roster. The Eagles are scheduled to host the Carolina Panthers in Week 6 action on Sunday. From NFL plays to college sports scores, all the top sports news you need to know every day. NFL WEEK 6: Game picks, odds and expert predictions for every matchup How Joe Milton fits with Eagles after Jalen Hurts injury The Eagles announced on Thursday that Hurts has a "superficial blood clot," that he is believed to have suffered during the team's Oct. 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams . He was cleared to play in Philadelphia's Oct. 11 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, England, before a follow-up ultrasound "revealed movement in the small blood clot." That led the Eagles to shut Hurts down for the immediate future. Before acquiring Milton, back-up Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton were the only other quarterbacks listed on the Philadelphia roster. McKee, 26, is slated to be the starter under center in Week 6 for the Eagles. He was the starting quarterback during the final game of the Eagles' regular season in each of the past two years and had a 1-1 record in those appearances. Payton was Philadelphia's fifth-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. If McGee were to falter and Hurts' absence forces an injured reserve stint, Milton could have an opportunity to start some games in Philadelphia. He's long been an intriguing developmental prospect because of his arm strength and could offer a downfield passing element to an offense that has struggled to generate explosive plays. Milton has never started an NFL game and has five career regular-season appearances over two seasons with the Patriots and Cowboys. Most of Milton's experience has come in the preseason, including several impressive moments in August with Dallas. Milton completed more than 67% of his passes over three 2026 exhibition games for 378 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. It included an eye-popping performance in his lone preseason start on Aug. 22 against the Arizona Cardinals in which he completed 9 of 13 passes for 179 yards and accounted for three touchdowns (two passing, one rushing). He won't be a long-term answer due to inconsistency and accuracy issues that have cropped up throughout his career. But Milton has shown enough promise to become a helpful stopgap until Hurts is back. It's a relatively low-risk move for the Eagles. home.blurb: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs will be eligible to return for his team's Week 7 game against the Detroit Lions despite the NFL's ongoing investigation into his conduct. It's unclear what the NFL will suspend Jacobs in the future after the investigation is complete. The games he misses while on the commissioner's exempt list will count toward whatever potential suspension the league could decide to hand down. The running back would also have to return the salary he earned while on the exempt list and remain unpaid throughout any suspension. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: When will Josh Jacobs return? Packers RB will be removed from exempt list "The National Football League today notified Josh Jacobs of the Green Bay Packers that he will be removed from the Commissioner Exempt List on Oct. 19," the league said in a statement. "He will be eligible to play in the Packers' Week 7 game on Oct. 25 after missing six games." Jacobs has been on the commissioner's exempt list since Aug. 30 after he was charged with two misdemeanors – one for battery, one for criminal damage to property. Those charges stemmed from an arrest in May following an incident involving the 28-year-old and his ex-girlfriend. From NFL plays to college sports scores, all the top sports news you need to know every day. Jacobs reached a plea deal in September, but the NFL's investigation is still ongoing. That is likely due in part to the league's desire to see video of the incident that led to Jacobs' arrest. "The NFL initiated an investigation under the Personal Conduct Policy following Jacobs' arrest in May," the league's Oct. 16 statement said. "The league's review remains ongoing and is not affected by this change to Jacobs' roster status." Attempts by Jacobs and his ex-girlfriend, who is not named in court documents, to seal the evidence have been unsuccessful so far, opening the door for the league to pursue legal avenues to obtain the footage. Meanwhile, Wisconsin police are delaying the release of video evidence cited in the criminal investigation into Jacobs' alleged domestic assault to requesting parties, including USA TODAY Sports. Jacobs and his ex-girlfriend filed separate injunctions against the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department on Oct. 14 in an attempt to stop the police from releasing records to the public. “Josh has dedicated the last several months to bettering himself, and he accepts responsibility for his actions," his attorneys, Clarence F. picks.blurb: Commanders vs. 49ers bold predictions for Week 6 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Commanders vs. 49ers bold predictions for Week 6 Monday Night Football Steven Bisig-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Wed, October 14, 2026 at 1:54 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads While the Washington Commanders are likely playing with a lame-duck coach, the San Francisco 49ers will be without a key defender. These teams, going in different directions, will meet in Week 6 on Monday Night Football, and here are bold predictions for the contest. Still reeling from a last-second overtime mental meltdown in the 27-27 tie to the Giants, the Commanders carry a record of 1-3-1 and a heavy underdog role into this game. Meanwhile, the 49ers are flying high with a record of 5-0 on the season. They're coming off an exciting 32-29 win over the Seahawks, giving them firm control of the NFC West title chase. 49ers QB Brock Purdy will throw for 300 yards The Commanders have been good against the run this season, giving up only 95.4 yards per game. They will have a challenge against the 49ers' offense, who are No. 8 in rushing yards per game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Look for the Commanders to slow, not stop, Christian McCaffrey. However, that opens things up for the 49ers' passing attack to hit high gear. The biggest problem the Commanders will have is Mike Evans. That's not a deep analysis. It's something every team faces when playing the 49ers. Purdy said Evans makes a big difference , according to ESPN. "He's a game changer," Purdy said after the win over the Seahawks. "True X receiver that, if you get the right look and stuff and you give him a chance, he can make defenses pay. "I thought today he did a great job with that, going up and getting the ball multiple times and just using his length and everything to create some separation. So as a quarterback, any time I have an (opportunity) to go to him, it always feels good." Evans doesn't shy away from the attention. And why should he? He's a future Hall of Famer. "I do feel like I'm one of the best receivers in the game," Evans said. "I got a big frame, so if you throw it around me, I'm going to do my best to try to make those contested grabs." The 49ers won't have Deebo Samuel, who suffered a hamstring injury against the Seahawks. That could allow the Commanders to focus more attention on Evans. But the 49ers still have threats, including George Kittle. And even Kittle has major respect for Evans, according to a post on X. "Mike Evans is really good at football," Kittle posted. 49ers TE George Kittle will have a season-high reception total Kittle's best game came in Week 3 against the Cardinals as he grabbed six passes for 82 yards and a pair of scores. Look for him to have a similar line against the Commanders with Samuel on the shelf. The 49ers have Kittle, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, and Jacob Cowing on the roster. And that's enough , said head coach Kyle Shanahan, according to ESPN. "I think we have enough," Shanahan said. "We've got three guys on practice squad also who can help. I mean, anytime you lose this number of guys, whether it's four guys or five guys, whatever it is, it's a huge challenge. But we do have guys in this building who can do it, and we'll always look." Commanders QB Jayden Daniels will finally cross 200-yard passing mark In three games this season, Daniels hasn't totaled over 200 yards passing. Look for that to change against the 49ers. It makes sense for the 49ers to focus defensively on keeping Daniels in check as a runner. He's coming off a game where he ran for 103 yards on nine carries and a pair of touchdowns. And look for the Commanders' game plan to lean more on the passing game than it has so far this season. Part of it will likely be from necessity as the Commanders figure to be chasing points throughout this game. Daniels has a lot to prove after his late-game blunder against the Giants. He has tried to own the situation , according to ESPN. "We have to stop the clock," Daniels said. "We have to know the situation. We have to relay that as an offense. It starts with everyone, top down. Ultimately, it's on me." A bounce-back game against the 49ers by Daniels won't help Quinn's future as head coach. But it would be an olive branch to Commanders' fans who are furious about Daniels' mental meltdown. Commanders WR Terry McLaurin will get a long TD Look for the Commanders to strike deep against the 49ers. McLaurin should be the beneficiary with a 40-plus-yard score. McLaurin hasn't been anything special from a fantasy perspective this season. He had catch totals of 2, 2, 6, and 4 in his first four games. He has 203 total yards and one touchdown. Those aren't WR1 numbers. He is playing like a pedestrian blob so far this season. And while he probably won't juice up those numbers much against the 49ers' tough defense, it's not out of the realm of possibility for him to get a deep ball. How big of an ask is a 40-yard TD strike between Daniels and McLaurin? Consider that Daniels' longest pass of the season is 33 yards. McLaurin's longest catch is 30 yards. Those numbers seem to belie the likelihood of a long hookup. However, the 49ers can't fear the deep ball because of this duo's modest production. And that's why there's a window of opportunity for a bomb. However, look for the Commanders to fall to 1-4-1 after this one. They don't have the roster to compete with the 49ers. San Francisco enters the Week 6 matchup at 5-0 after an exciting 32-29 road victory over the Seattle Seahawks, while Washington arrives at 1-3-1 following a frustrating 27-27 overtime tie against the New York Giants. The matchup presents two teams heading in different directions. The 49ers have found ways to win close games, while the Commanders are searching for consistency as they attempt to climb back into the NFC playoff conversation. Kickoff is scheduled for 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN and ABC. Brock Purdy Leads San Francisco's Offense Quarterback Brock Purdy has helped guide the 49ers through an impressive opening stretch. Although San Francisco has faced several challenging opponents, the offense has continued producing at important moments. Purdy threw two touchdown passes against Seattle and helped lead the game-winning drive that set up Eddy Piñeiro's decisive field goal. His ability to distribute the football and make smart decisions has been important to the team's success. Running back Christian McCaffrey remains another major weapon. His versatility as both a runner and receiver gives head coach Kyle Shanahan several ways to attack opposing defenses. San Francisco will look to establish its running game early, create favorable passing situations and control the tempo. The 49ers' offense has also benefited from contributions across the roster, allowing the team to remain productive even when individual drives become difficult. Jayden Daniels Looks to Spark Washington Washington will rely on quarterback Jayden Daniels to help generate offense against a San Francisco defense that has started the season strongly. Daniels demonstrated his playmaking ability against the Giants, rushing for 103 yards and two touchdowns while throwing for 199 yards. However, Washington's inability to finish the game left the team with a disappointing tie. Daniels' mobility could be one of the Commanders' biggest advantages. San Francisco will need disciplined defensive play to prevent him from escaping the pocket and creating explosive gains with his legs. Washington also needs better protection up front and more consistent execution on third downs. Sustaining drives will be particularly important against a 49ers team that has repeatedly capitalized on scoring opportunities. Kyle Shanahan vs. Dan Quinn The coaching matchup adds another layer to Monday night's game. Shanahan has San Francisco playing confident football, while Quinn needs Washington to respond after letting a potential victory slip away. For the Commanders, limiting turnovers and improving their second-half execution will be essential. The 49ers, meanwhile, will look to continue their balanced offensive approach and use their home-field advantage. A Major Test for Both Teams San Francisco has an opportunity to improve to 6-0 and strengthen its position in the NFC West. Washington needs a complete performance to show it can compete with one of the conference's unbeaten teams. With Purdy and McCaffrey leading the 49ers against Daniels and Washington's offense, Monday night's matchup offers an important test for both teams as the NFL season moves deeper into October.

By Michael Gallagher Sports Content Coordinator 0 Share Newsweek is a Trust Project member See more of our trusted coverage when you search. Prefer Newsweek on Google to see more of our trusted coverage when you search. The San Francisco 49ers have had arguably the worst injury luck of any team in the NFL this season. More than 15 players are currently on the reserve/injured list while a handful of others are expected to miss some time with their respective ailments. San Francisco’s defense has been hit particularly hard, and star edge-rusher Nick Bosa’s absence over the last few weeks has been noticeable. Keion White has done his part to pick up the slack, but the rest of San Francisco’s pass-rush has left much to be desired, which is why Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report believes the 49ers should make an all-in move to upgrade the position. Knox recently suggested the 49ers execute a trade with the winless Los Angeles Chargers for Pro Bowler Khalil Mack. “Los Angeles fell to 0-5 on Sunday, while Mack continues to be a legitimate difference-maker,” Knox wrote . “… Mack is playing on a one-year deal and should be interested in playing for a team that could get him his first career playoff win. “.. Mack should be the top target for any team with Super Bowl aspirations that happens to need help rushing opposing passers. It'll be a fairly significant surprise if he remains in Los Angeles beyond next month's deadline.” Despite multiple reports indicating the Chargers would want a fifth-round pick in exchange for Mack, Knox suggested it could take at least a conditional 2027 fourth-round pick to get a deal finalized given the demand for strong pass-rushers from contending teams. Through five games this season, Mack has logged 14 pressures, eight hurries, five tackles for loss, three QB hits, and three sacks with a pass-rush win-rate of 9.5%, according to Pro Football Focus. Adding that kind of production opposite White would be a big boost for the 49ers in the interim, and once Bosa comes back, it would make SF’s pass-rush all the more dangerous come playoff time.

home.headline: 49ers injury updates: Mike Evans nursing Achilles soreness
home.blurb: While their receiving corps remains banged up with wide receiver Deebo Samuel out multiple weeks with a hamstring injury, head coach Kyle Shanahan on Monday indicated defensive end Nick Bosa (knee, calf), fullback Kyle Juszczyk (knee) and defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. (ankle) all have a chance to return when the 49ers host Washington. Samuel isn't in line to play vs. the Commanders after suffering a hamstring injury in Week 6, but how long he'll be out remains a mystery. Shanahan indicated there's hope Samuel returns after the Week 8 Bye, but he also said the team isn't ruling out an IR stint . Tepid optimism about Nick Bosa return for Week 6 Shanahan on Monday said there was a chance Bosa would be able to play against the Commanders. He didn't rule it out Thursday, but his optimism didn't increase since he last spoke to reporters. Shanahan's pre-practice injury updates Thursday came with some dreadful news about the 49ers' veteran wide receiver. Evans will be out of Thursday's practice, the first of the week, with an Achilles issue Shanahan described as "Achilles soreness." Given Evans' injury history, this one will be worth monitoring very closely throughout the week. Playing through a rib injury is much different than playing through an Achilles issue. Shanahan on Sunday after the 49ers' win over the Seahawks was mum on a Kirk return. The veteran WR is dealing with a calf injury he suffered early in training camp. The 49ers on Thursday announced Kirk's practice window is open, giving the receiver a chance to return for Week 6 where he could help their ailing WR room. WR Deebo Samuel out for multiple weeks The San Francisco 49ers may be getting some injury luck on their side heading into a Week 6 matchup vs. the Washington Commanders . A Monday night game means the 49ers' practice week gets pushed back a day, so the typical Wednesday practice is moved to Thursday. The typical Thursday practice is moved to Friday, and then we'll get an official injury report Saturday. "Hoping he can go, but not able to practice today." Bosa strained his calf warming up for practice leading up to Week 3. He was due to miss "a few weeks." As of the end of Week 5 he'd missed three weeks. The odds seem long for him to play against Washington, and the team may not be in a hurry to rush him back with a 5-0 record and a Bye week awaiting in Week 8. 49ers projected practice participation for Thursday Shanahan gave a pre-practice participation report in his Thursday press conference. home.headline: 49ers vs. Commanders Preview: San Francisco Looks to Stay Undefeated
home.blurb: The San Francisco 49ers return home Monday night looking to extend their undefeated start when they host the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium. San Francisco enters the Week 6 matchup at 5-0 after an exciting 32-29 road victory over the Seattle Seahawks, while Washington arrives at 1-3-1 following a frustrating 27-27 overtime tie against the New York Giants. 49ers vs. Commanders Preview: San Francisco Looks to Stay Undefeated - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL 49ers vs. Commanders Preview: San Francisco Looks to Stay Undefeated Photo by: Darren Yamashita Stephan Stroud Fri, October 16, 2026 at 8:53 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads 49ers Aim to Keep Rolling on Monday Night The matchup presents two teams heading in different directions. The 49ers have found ways to win close games, while the Commanders are searching for consistency as they attempt to climb back into the NFC playoff conversation. Kickoff is scheduled for 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN and ABC. Brock Purdy Leads San Francisco's Offense Quarterback Brock Purdy has helped guide the 49ers through an impressive opening stretch. Although San Francisco has faced several challenging opponents, the offense has continued producing at important moments. Purdy threw two touchdown passes against Seattle and helped lead the game-winning drive that set up Eddy Piñeiro's decisive field goal. His ability to distribute the football and make smart decisions has been important to the team's success. Running back Christian McCaffrey remains another major weapon. His versatility as both a runner and receiver gives head coach Kyle Shanahan several ways to attack opposing defenses. San Francisco will look to establish its running game early, create favorable passing situations and control the tempo. The 49ers' offense has also benefited from contributions across the roster, allowing the team to remain productive even when individual drives become difficult. Jayden Daniels Looks to Spark Washington Washington will rely on quarterback Jayden Daniels to help generate offense against a San Francisco defense that has started the season strongly. Daniels demonstrated his playmaking ability against the Giants, rushing for 103 yards and two touchdowns while throwing for 199 yards. However, Washington's inability to finish the game left the team with a disappointing tie. Daniels' mobility could be one of the Commanders' biggest advantages. San Francisco will need disciplined defensive play to prevent him from escaping the pocket and creating explosive gains with his legs. Washington also needs better protection up front and more consistent execution on third downs. Sustaining drives will be particularly important against a 49ers team that has repeatedly capitalized on scoring opportunities. The coaching matchup adds another layer to Monday night's game.
